D 8939 A/9:
File No. ________
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I. Special Branch Stability /
REPORT
Date October 15, 1938.
Subject (in full) Suspected Chinese Traitor assaulted.
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by 〔此处转录不清〕
On October 14, a male Chinese, who disembarked from a
steam launch at the Roosevelt Terminal, was beaten and
thrown into the Whangpoo by a crowd on the wharf, because
he was seen disembarking from a launch which had come from
a Japanese battleship. He was later rescued and taken to
the French Police Station by a French Police constable on
duty in the vicinity.
Pan Lien-pih
D. I.
D.C. (Special Branch).
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 17.10.38）

特别情报科 稳定 /
报告
日期：1938年10月15日。
主题（全称）：疑似中国汉奸遭殴打。
呈报人：督察潘连璧 转呈人：〔此处转录不清〕
10月14日，一名中国男子在罗斯福码头（Roosevelt Terminal）从一艘蒸汽小艇上岸时，被码头上的人群殴打并抛入黄浦江，原因是有人看见他从一艘来自日本战舰的小艇上下来。他随后被附近执勤的一名法国巡捕救起，并送往法国警察局。
潘连璧
督察
副警司（特别情报科）。

to become the supreme power in East Asia and finally to
attempt to conquer the whole world. Such declarations
have exposed to us all the plots of the enemy for the
subjugation of our country and the annihilation of our race.
The enemy is well-known for its trickery,
deliberate misinterpretation of facts and creating situations
disadvantageous to others. That this is not without
foundation is borne out by the fact that shortly after the
promulgation of Konoye's statement, another statement was
issued (on December 24) by the so-called spokesman of the
Japanese Government in which the opinion was
expressed that what the Premier had said constituted the
minimum demands that would be handed to China.
No doubt there exists a section of the world
which is still ignorant of the real intentions of the enemy
because of the smoke screen and which still holds the view
that the enemy's demands are not so harsh as expected.
Therefore I am going to expose to the public the real motives
harboured by Japan so as to warn all people and to enable
the friendly nations to understand Japan's ambitious designs
and treacherous plots.
Let us discuss separately the statement made
by the Japanese Premier Konoye on December 22 and the various
kinds of plots and slogans advocated by the Japanese
newspapers and actually accelerated by Japan during the
past few months with a view to acquiring a fair understanding
of Japan's real intentions. Before proceeding further,
I draw your attention to the following points:-

(1) The Establishment of a "New Order in East Asia"

This is the most favorite slogan of the
Japanese people. According to the explanation made by the
Japanese Foreign Minister Arita on December 19, the "new
order in East Asia" means close co-operation and mutual
aid in political, economic and cultural affairs among the
three nations, Japan, Manchukuo and China in order to
check the infiltration of communism, promote Asiatic
civilization and abolish economic obstacles among the three
countries so as to save China from becoming a semi-colony,
thereby ensuring peace in East Asia. In the course of
a speech made on December 14, Prince Konoye also said:
Japan's final objective in the China incident
does not depend solely upon military success but upon
the rebirth of China and the establishment of a "new
order in East Asia". This "new order" has as its
base the tripartite co-operation between Japan,
Manchukuo and China when "China's" revival has
become a fact.
It is significant that the so-called "rebirth
of China" advocated by Japan means the subjugation of an
independent China and its replacement with a slavish China
which can be placed under Japan's control forever, because
such a "new order" can be realized only after the conversion
of the present China into a slavish nation which will
closely co-operate with Japan and the Japanese sponsored
puppet state of Manchukuo. Its purposes are the seizure
of control of military affairs in China, the crushing of the

成为东亚的至高权力，并最终企图征服整个世界。此类声明向我们所有人暴露了敌人征服我国和灭绝我民族的阴谋。敌人以诡计多端、故意曲解事实以及制造对他方不利的局势而闻名。这并非毫无根据，近卫声明颁布后不久，所谓日本政府发言人又发表了一份声明（12月24日），其中表示首相所言构成了将向中国提出的最低要求。
毫无疑问，世界上仍有一部分人因受烟幕弹迷惑而不了解敌人的真实意图，仍认为敌人的要求并不像预期的那样苛刻。因此，我将向公众揭露日本怀有的真实动机，以警示所有民众，并使友好国家了解日本的野心设计和奸诈阴谋。
让我们分别讨论日本首相近卫于12月22日发表的声明，以及日本报纸在过去几个月中鼓吹并由日本实际加速推进的各种阴谋和口号，以便对日本的真实意图有一个公正的了解。在进一步阐述之前，提请诸位注意以下几点：-

(1) 建立“东亚新秩序”

这是日本人最喜爱的口号。根据日本外相有田于12月19日所作的解释，“东亚新秩序”意味着日本、满洲国和中国三国在政治、经济和文化事务上的紧密合作与互助，以遏制共产主义的渗透，促进亚洲文明，消除三国之间的经济障碍，从而使中国免于沦为半殖民地，进而确保东亚和平。近卫亲王在12月14日的一次演讲中也说道：
日本在事变中的最终目标不仅取决于军事胜利，还取决于中国的重生和“东亚新秩序”的建立。这个“新秩序”的基础是当“中国”复兴成为事实时，日本、满洲国和中国之间的三方合作。
值得注意的是，日本所鼓吹的所谓“中国重生”，意味着使独立的中国屈服，并将其替换为一个可以永远置于日本控制之下的奴役性中国，因为只有在将当前的中国转变为一个与日本及日本扶植的傀儡政权满洲国紧密合作的奴役性民族之后，这种“新秩序”才能实现。其目的是夺取对中国军事事务的控制权，粉碎中

Chinese nation and culture, the removal of European
and American influences and privileges from this country
and supremacy in the Pacific under the cloak of promoting
anti-Communism and Asiatic civilization and removing
all economic obstacles among the three nations, Japan,
Manchukuo and China; another object is the control of
Chinese economic resources by the "Japan-Manchukuo-China
Economic Unit or Economic Mission." One can thus imagine
what a dangerous situation "the establishment of a new
order in East Asia" will give rise to. To put it shortly,
the principal object is the impairment of international
peace in East Asia and the conversion of China into a
slavish nation so that Japan may acquire supremacy in
the Pacific and have a free hand in the world.

(to be continued)

Shun Pao :-

THE BLOCKADE OF THE YANGTZE RIVER : FOREIGN RESIDENTS
REQUEST DEFENCE FORCE AUTHORITIES TO PROTEST

The Joint Committee formed by local
British, American, French and nationals of four other
Powers held a meeting at the British Chamber of Commerce
on the evening of last Wednesday to discuss the blockade
of the Yangtze River by the Japanese.

As a result of the discussions, it was
resolved to request the British and American Consulates
to lodge, in conjunction with their defence force
authorities in Shanghai, another protest with the Japanese
military authorities, to demand that a trial resumption
of navigation between Shanghai and Nanking be allowed
as soon as possible and that the line be afterwards
extended to Anhui. If the Japanese authorities continue to
raise objections, a round table conference may be called
at a British or American flagship to consider the
situation.

It is learned that both the British
and American Consuls and their defence forces in Shanghai
have received this request from local foreign residents,
and the matter is under consideration.

华民族和文化，消除欧美在这个国家的影响和特权，并在促进反共主义和亚洲文明以及消除日本、满洲国和中国三国之间所有经济障碍的幌子下，确立在太平洋的霸权；另一个目的是通过“日满华经济集团或经济使团”控制中国的经济资源。由此可以想象，“建立东亚新秩序”将引发多么危险的局势。简而言之，其主要目标是破坏东亚的国际和平，将中国变为奴役性国家，以便日本获得在太平洋的霸权并在世界上为所欲为。

《申报》：

长江封锁：外籍居民请求防卫部队当局提出抗议

由当地英、美、法及其他四个强国国民组成的联合委员会，于上周三晚在英国商会举行会议，讨论日本对长江的封锁问题。

经讨论，决议请求英美领事馆与其在上海的防卫部队当局联合，再次向日本军方当局提出抗议，要求尽快允许恢复上海与南京之间的航运试行，随后将该航线延伸至安徽。如果日本当局继续提出异议，可在英国或美国旗舰上召开圆桌会议以审议局势。

据悉，驻上海的英美领事及其防卫部队已收到当地外籍居民的这一请求，此事正在审议中。

December 30, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Jan Feo and other local newspapers dated December 29
(Chungking telegram) :-

"JAPAN'S PLOTS TO CONQUER THE WHOLE OF CHINA EXPOSED
BY GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK"

(Continued from Morning Translation)

(2) The so-called "collective co-operation in East Asia,"
the "non-separation of Japan, Manchukuo and China"
and the "mutual relations for co-operation among
Japan, Manchukuo and China". -

The so-called "collective co-operation in
East Asia" is a slogan that has been loudly advocated
by the enemy during the past few months. To tell the
truth, it aims at the complete subjugation of China and
her amalgamation with the North East as one unit, not
only politically but also economically and culturally on
the ground that Japan, Manchukuo and China are inseparable.
Japanese newspapers and magazines have even openly declared
that under the plan of "collective co-operation in East
Asia," Japan should assume the parental role in the family
of the three nations, while Manchukuo and China should
act as her subordinates. In other words, Japan is to be
the master, while Manchukuo and China are to serve as
slaves. Does not all this mean the complete enslavement
of China?

Last month, a very ridiculous and absurd
statement was made by the Japanese Premier Konoye. He
advocated the establishment of mutual relations for
political, economic and cultural co-operation among Japan,
Manchukuo and China. What does it mean? The so-called
"mutual relations for political, economic and cultural
co-operation among Japan, Manchukuo and China" resembles
the lock of a handcuff; that is to say, that by means of
these relations, the entire Chinese nation will be placed
under Japan's control forever as in the case of a prisoner
locked with a handcuff.

(3) The "economic unit" and "economic mission"

This already has been advocated in Japan
for several years and is now being widely promoted and
accelerated. Frankly speaking, it is one of the essential
factors in the acceleration of the movement for "collective
co-operation in East Asia." Sometimes it is called
economic rapprochement or economic co-operation. In the
manifesto issued by the Japanese Government on November 4,
it was referred to as "economic connection." At the end
of November, articles headed "Economic Unit to be Proclaimed
among Japan, Manchukuo and China - Hereafter They will
Bear Equal Privileges and Share Equal Disadvantages"
appeared in enemy newspapers. In amplification, the
Japanese Foreign Minister Arita, in the course of a
statement on December 19, declared that Japan had decided
to convene an economic conference to bring about closer

12月29日的《辛日报》（Sin Jan Feo，音译）及其他当地报纸（重庆电）：

“蒋介石将军揭露日本征服全中国的阴谋”

（接上午译文）

(2) 所谓的“东亚集体合作”、“日满华不可分离”以及“日满华合作关系”。-

所谓的“东亚集体合作”是敌人在过去几个月中大力鼓吹的口号。说实话，其目的是以日满华不可分离为由，不仅在政治上，而且在经济和文化上将中国与东北合并为一个整体，从而完全征服中国。日本报刊甚至公开宣称，在“东亚集体合作”计划下，日本应在三国大家庭中扮演家长角色，而满洲国和中国则应充当其下属。换言之，日本为主人，而满洲国和中国为奴隶。这一切难道不意味着对中国的完全奴役吗？

上月，日本首相近卫发表了一项非常荒谬和无稽的声明。他主张建立日本、满洲国和中国之间在政治、经济和文化方面的合作关系。这意味着什么？所谓的“日满华政治、经济和文化合作关系”类似于手铐的锁扣；也就是说，通过这些关系，整个中华民族将像被手铐锁住的囚犯一样，永远置于日本的控制之下。

(3) “经济集团”和“经济使团”

这在日本已鼓吹数年，目前正被广泛推广和加速。坦率地说，它是加速“东亚集体合作”运动的基本因素之一。有时它被称为经济亲善或经济合作。在日本政府11月4日发布的宣言中，它被称为“经济联系”。11月底，敌伪报纸上出现了题为“日满华将宣布成立经济集团——此后他们将享有同等权利并分担同等不利条件”的文章。作为补充，日本外相有田在12月19日的声明中宣布，日本决定召开一次经济会议，以促进

economic co-operation among Japan, Manchukuo and China
with a view to enforcing an "economic unit" among the
three countries. Such economic relations as advocated
by Japan are generally called an "economic mission,"
but in the eyes of Japan, they are used as an instrument
to exploit the economic resources of this country. The
North China and the South China Development Companies
have already been established, while the Japan-Manchukuo-
China Economic Conference has already met more than once.
Moreover, the "Enterprise Planning Bureau" has already
started planning for the development of production in
Japan, Manchukuo and China. The "economic mission" as
advocated by Japan aims not only at monopolizing the
control of our economic resources and Customs revenue
and harming our productive force and commerce but also
at acquiring hegemony in East Asia, with the ultimate
result that we will completely lose our freedom and we all
will be at the mercy of the Japanese, and the Chinese
nation will become enslaved and her people will have to
work like beasts under whip.

(4) The establishment of a so-called "Asiatic Reconstruc-
tion Bureau"

This Bureau was established only after
much discussion over the formation of a special organ to
deal with China. It was originally planned to have it
known as the "Chinese Affairs Bureau," but later the
present title was retained. The former name was already
sufficiently insulting but the change is even worse for
it constitutes a gross insult to the peoples of the
whole Asiatic Continent. Japan's aim in establishing
such a bureau is undoubtedly to bring about the
disintegration and the subjugation of China and to
expand her influence in Asia. That this surmise is not
without foundation is proved by the statement made by
Prince Konoye on December 15, the day prior to the
formal inauguration of this bureau, in which he said
with emphasis:-
"A desire is now being felt to start
preparations for the formation of a new executive
organ to bring about the establishment of a 'new
order in East Asia.' This organ, when it comes
into being, will maintain mutual contact with all
the Japanese organs abroad and will constitute
the centre for the acceleration of the policy
vis-a-vis China, so as to bring about the
realization of Japan's ultimate object in the
China incident."
This, I think, will enlighten you as to
Japan's real intentions in creating such an organ.
Briefly, it will be the headquarters which looks after
the execution of all Japan's plans for the subjugation
of China. Actually, it has all the earmarks of a General
Headquarters of the Japanese Special Service Organs in

日本、满洲国和中国之间更紧密的经济合作，旨在在三国间实施“经济集团”。日本所鼓吹的这种经济关系通常被称为“经济使团”，但在日本眼中，它们被用作剥削我国经济资源的工具。华北和华南开发公司已经成立，而日满华经济会议也已召开多次。此外，“企业规划局”已开始规划日本、满洲国和中国的生产发展。日本所鼓吹的“经济使团”不仅旨在垄断对我国经济资源和关税收入的控制，损害我国的生产力和商业，还旨在获取东亚霸权，最终结果是我们将完全失去自由，我们都将任日本人摆布，中华民族将被奴役，其人民将不得不像牲畜一样在鞭子下劳作。

(4) 建立所谓的“亚洲复兴局”

该局是在就设立处理中国事务的专门机构进行大量讨论后才成立的。原计划将其命名为“对华事务局”，但后来保留了现在的名称。前一个名称已足够具有侮辱性，但更改后的名称更甚，因为它构成了对整个亚洲大陆人民的严重侮辱。日本建立这样一个局的目的无疑是为了导致中国的分裂和屈服，并扩大其在亚洲的影响力。这一推测并非毫无根据，近卫亲王在该局正式揭幕前一天（12月15日）发表的声明证明了这一点，他在声明中强调说：-
“现在人们感到有必要开始筹备组建一个新的执行机构，以实现‘东亚新秩序’的建立。该机构一旦成立，将与所有日本海外机构保持相互联系，并构成加速对华政策的中心，从而实现日本在事变中的最终目标。”
我想，这将使你们明白日本创建这样一个机构的真实意图。简而言之，它将成为负责执行日本所有征服中国计划的总部。实际上，它具有日本在华特务机关总司令部的所有特征。

China. The establishment of the Asiatic Reconstruction
Bureau has shown us more clearly Japan's attitude
towards China, her ultimate motive in the Sino-Japanese
incident and what she really desires from us. Whilst

But what are the things which Japan

planning the enslavement of China. Japan will never
cease her ambitious designs until she has realized
her object.

亚洲复兴局的建立更清楚地向我们展示了日本对华态度、其在事变中的最终动机以及它真正想从我们这里得到什么。当我们主张持久抵抗时，日本人则在推动持久复兴。
但是，日本想要复兴的是什么？简而言之，她正在策划对中国的奴役。日本在实现其目标之前，绝不会停止其野心设计。

（待续）

January 4, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Po and other local newspapers dated December 29,
1938 (Chungking telegram) :-

"JAPAN'S PLOTS TO CONQUER THE WHOLE OF CHINA EXPOSED
BY GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK"

(Continued from Dec. 30, 1938)

With a proper understanding of the points
given above, we will then be able to realize, without
mistake, the real meaning of the statement made by
Japanese Premier Konoye on December 22. I draw your
attention to the following points in his statement:-
(1) His principal object in making this
statement is to bring about co-operation among Japan,
Manchukuo and China in establishing a new order in East
Asia; he ostensibly desires to make known to the Powers
and China the sincere intentions of the Japanese
Government. It is for this reason that the statement
was couched in very careful and discreet terms. He
states that what Japan desires from China is not
territory nor a war indemnity nor privileges; Japan
desires only peace in the whole of East Asia. He even
said that Japan is anxious to enable China to become an
absolutely independent nation and she was even willing
to consider the abolition of her extraterritoriality
and the return of her concessions, etc. All this would
seem to indicate that Japan really has no evil designs
upon China, that she is even willing to give something
to China. In the opinion of the Japanese Premier, the
world seems to be still unaware of her real intentions
in regard to the so-called new order in East Asia
advocated by him. To tell the truth, Japan's intentions
in advocating the so-called co-operation among Japan,
Manchukuo and China and the new order in East Asia are
clear and are as I have just said a little while ago.
With the object of conquering the whole of China and
acquiring hegemony in East Asia, Japan naturally deems
it unnecessary to demand any further territory or war
indemnity as what she really desires is the whole of
this country. She wants territory and resources that
can be placed under her absolute control. She says that
she desires no territory nor war indemnity from China
only with the object of deceiving the world.
Now from the Chinese point of view, it is
necessary to ascertain who is responsible for the
outbreak of the present hostilities before any question
of war indemnity can be considered. As it is known to
all that the present conflict was started by Japan
herself to accelerate her invasion of our territory, she
has naturally to bear the responsibility of the incident
as she is the aggressor. Therefore, what Prince Konoye
said in his statement regarding this question deserves
no consideration. As regards extraterritoriality, if
Japan is allowed to enjoy this system in China, then
the integrity of the sovereign rights of this country
will amount to nothing. The so-called "return of
concessions in China" is but empty talk, in view of the

1939年1月4日。下午译件。

《新报》及其他本地报纸，1938年12月29日刊（重庆电）：-

“蒋介石将军揭露日本征服全中国之阴谋”

（续自1938年12月30日）

正确理解上述各点之后，我们便能毫无差错地领会日本首相近卫于12月22日所发表声明的真实含义。提请诸位注意其声明中的以下几点：-
(1) 他发表此声明的主要目的，是促成日本、满洲国与中国之间的合作，以建立东亚新秩序；他表面上希望向列强及中国表明日本政府的诚意。正因如此，该声明措辞极为谨慎和含蓄。他声称，日本对中国所求者，非领土，非战争赔款，亦非特权；日本所求者，唯全东亚之和平。他甚至表示，日本急于使中国成为一个完全独立的国家，甚至愿意考虑废除其在华治外法权并归还租界等。这一切似乎表明，日本确实对中国并无恶意，甚至愿意给予中国某些利益。在日本首相看来，世界似乎仍未察觉他就其所倡导的所谓“东亚新秩序”的真正意图。说实话，日本倡导所谓日、满、中合作及东亚新秩序的意图是明确的，正如我刚才所述。既然其目的在于征服全中国并在东亚取得霸权，日本自然认为无需再索取任何领土或战争赔款，因为她真正想要的是这个国家的全部。她想要的是能置于其绝对控制之下的领土和资源。她声称不向中国索取领土或战争赔款，仅是为了欺骗世界。
现在从中国方面来看，在考虑任何战争赔款问题之前，有必要查明谁应对当前敌对行动的爆发负责。众所周知，当前的冲突是由日本自身为加速入侵我国领土而发动的，因此作为侵略者，她自然必须承担事件的责任。因此，近卫亲王在声明中关于此问题的言论不值一顾。至于治外法权，如果允许日本在中国享有这一制度，那么该国主权的完整将荡然无存。所谓的“归还中国在沪租界”不过是空谈，鉴于

among Japan, Manchukuo and China for the establishment
of a new order in East Asia, it is tantamount to making
all Chinese territory into a large Japanese Concession.
By so doing, China will have to become a Japanese colony
or at best a Japanese protectorate. In other words,
China will have to become part and parcel of Japan.
The real intention of the Japanese Premier when he said
in his statement that he intended to help China to become
an absolutely independent nation is but to make China
a second Korea as defined in the Sino-Japanese Agreement
concluded at Peking. I am confident that before the
promulgation of the present statement of Prince Konoye, .
there may have been certain people in the world who were
expecting that Japan would repent of her present
activities in China, but with the publication of
this statement no Chinese who is well aware of present
international conditions and is loyal to the nation will
ever entertain any hope of compromise with Japan.
(2) Besides the above, Konoye's statement
also advocates economic rapprochement and joint action
against communism. It is unnecessary to amplify the
aim of the so-called "economic rapprochement" which was
clearly explained in my previous speech referring to the
economic mission. The so-called "joint action against

Comintern Pact with Japan; that Japan has the right to
station garrison forces in North China and that Inner

unanimously working in accordance with the Three
Principles of the People, it would be far from our
objective to discuss any further joint action against
communism. To tell the truth, Japan's real object is to
seize control of our military affairs to be followed
by our political and cultural as well as diplomatic
affairs under the pretext of the so-called "joint action
against communism." This can be called the principal
cause of Japan's vengeance against us for our repeated
refusal to her demands prior to the outbreak of the
Lukouchiao incident. It is because we were unwilling
to fall into Japan's trap that we have put a united front

China could have agreed to Japan's demand for joint
action against communism, there would have been
no need for us to wait until the present. The world
may be of the opinion that the so-called "joint action
against communism" advocated by Japan is really intended
to deal with Soviet Russia; actually, however, Japan's
desire to enter into an anti-Comintern Pact with China
is not aimed at communism nor at Soviet Russia but at
the subjugation of China under this pretext. Even if

事实是，日本人及其报纸甚至鼓动和煽动控制该国所有外国租界，以便将其转化为一个巨大的日本租界。因此，简而言之，如果中国同意日本提出的日、满、中合作建立东亚新秩序的计划，这就等同于将所有中国领土变成一个巨大的日本租界。这样做，中国将被迫成为日本的殖民地，或者至多成为日本的保护国。换句话说，中国将成为日本的一部分。日本首相在声明中表示有意帮助中国成为一个完全独立的国家，其真实意图不过是使中国成为根据在北京签订的中日协定所定义的第二个朝鲜。我有信心，在近卫亲王发表当前声明之前，世界上可能有一些人期待日本会对其在华目前的行径悔悟，但随着该声明的发布，任何熟知当前国际形势且忠于国家的中国人，都不会再抱有与日本妥协的任何希望。
(2) 此外，近卫的声明还倡导经济亲善和联合防共。所谓“经济亲善”的目的在我此前关于经济代表团的讲话中已作清楚解释，无需赘述。所谓“联合防共”意味着中国应与日本缔结反共产国际协定；日本有权在华北驻军，并将内蒙古划定为防共特殊区域。现在，撇开所谓“联合防共”的实际动机不谈，在当前举国一致遵循三民主义之际，进一步讨论任何联合防共行动都与我们的目标相去甚远。说实话，日本的真正目的是借所谓“联合防共”之名，夺取对我国军事事务的控制权，继而控制我国的政治、文化以及外交事务。这可以说是日本因我们在卢沟桥事变爆发前多次拒绝其要求而对我们进行报复的主要原因。正是因为我们不愿落入日本的陷阱，尽管遭受巨大的牺牲和苦难，我们还是建立了抗日统一战线。如果中国当时能同意日本关于联合防共的要求，我们就无需等到今天。世人可能认为日本所倡导的所谓“联合防共”确实是针对苏联俄罗斯；然而实际上，日本希望与中国缔结反共产国际协定，其目标并非共产主义，也非苏联俄罗斯，而是借此借口征服中国。即使

Japan really had the intention to deal with the U.S.S.R.,
this but constitutes a minor part of the plan, the major
part being the enslavement of China. If this is not
the case, or if Japan's real intention is actually for
her national defence and to deal with Soviet Russia,
then why was Shigemitsu, the Japanese Ambassador to
Soviet Russia, so submissive to the Soviet Foreign
Commissar at the time of the Changkaofeng incident in
July and August last year (1938)? From this we can see
quite clearly that Japan's demand at the present time
for joint action against communism is but a smoke screen
to deceive the world as well as her own people and is
aimed at securing the right to station forces in North
China and Inner Mongolia. If China could agree to the
garrisoning of Japanese forces in North China and to the
demarcation of Inner Mongolia into a special area for
anti-communist purposes, we would not have started the
present war of resistance at the time of the outbreak of
the Lukouchiao incident. If China could tolerate Japanese
control of North China because of fear of Japan, then
at the time when Tanaka sent an expeditionary force to
Tsinan in the 17th Year (1928) of the Chinese Republic,
the Chinese revolutionary forces would not have dared
to push on their drive to Peiping. That Japan can have
made such a demand at the present time shows that she
still lacks good understanding of the present China as
well as of the existing circumstances. According to
the Japanese Premier's statement, unless Japan has the
right to station troops in North China and Inner
Mongolia, there is no hope for the realization of the
establishment of a new order in East Asia. I think that
this will be sufficient to enlighten the world as to
what the so-called "new order in East Asia" really means.

日本确实有意对付苏联，这也只是计划的一小部分，主要部分乃是奴役中国。若非如此，或者说如果日本的真实意图确实是为了其国防和对付苏联，那么为何在去年（1938年）七八月间的张鼓峰事件期间，日本驻苏大使重光葵对苏联外交人民委员如此卑躬屈膝？由此我们可以清楚地看到，日本目前要求联合防共不过是一个欺骗世界及其本国人民的烟幕弹，其目的是确保在华北和内蒙古驻军的权利。如果中国能同意日军在华北驻军并将内蒙古划定为防共特殊区域，我们就不会在卢沟桥事变爆发时开始目前的抗战。如果中国因畏惧日本而容忍其对华北的控制，那么在中华民国十七年（1928年）田中派远征军前往济南时，中国革命军队就不敢继续向北平推进。日本如今能提出这样的要求，表明她对当今中国及现有局势仍缺乏良好的了解。根据日本首相的声明，除非日本拥有在华北和内蒙古驻军的权利，否则建立东亚新秩序的希望就无法实现。我认为，这足以让世人明白所谓“东亚新秩序”的真正含义。

international order, secure hegemony in East Asia and
remove all American and European influences from the

of throwing dust in the eyes of the world. This is

1938年12月1日举行的日本政府枢密院会议上，近卫亲王称：“中国事变的结束取决于中国重建工作的进展。”所谓“中国重建工作的进展”，换言之，就是日本在征服本国工作中取得的进展。这使我们确信，日本在成功征服我国之前，绝不会停止对中国的侵略行为。至此，世界必须充分认识到，日本的政策已经从大陆扩张到海洋，北进政策也已转变为南进政策。简言之，日本目前的侵略政策旨在扩大其在亚洲大陆及太平洋沿岸的影响力，也就是说，在试图征服中国的同时，它还意图推翻国际秩序，确立在东亚的霸权，并清除美欧在远东的所有影响。日本在实现这一目标后将做什么，是一个众所周知的公开秘密。总之，近卫的声明向全世界揭露了日本在过去几十年里所怀有的所有野心希望和邪恶图谋。
我相信，此后世界将充分信服日本的野心图谋。简要研究近卫的声明就会使我们相信，日本的真正目的是征服本国，彻底奴役我们的民族，而非中日合作或经济亲善。在日本看来，战争赔款或割让部分中国领土的问题是无足轻重的。日本所倡导的经济使命，意味着以控制中国所有经济资源来代替索取战争赔款的要求；而其要求在华北和内蒙古驻军以及在全国范围内享有居住和经商自由的权利，则是意图以控制中国全境和压迫、奴役中国人民来代替索取部分中国领土的要求。
人们还记得，在日本吞并朝鲜之前，日本人也曾宣扬日朝同种、日朝不可分离等论调，其目的是欺骗朝鲜人民。现在，他们又在“日满华不可分”的口号下倡导东亚集体合作。更明确地说，东亚集体合作意味着中国与日本合并；换言之，这意味着日本吞并中国并实现其大陆帝国。为了掩盖这些阴谋，近卫亲王在声明中称，这一切都是为了建立东亚新秩序。他说这话是希望迷惑世人的眼睛。这是

page_data.en:
a new method invented by the Japanese Imperialists for
the subjugation of China and the annihilation of the
Chinese people. Japan has now prepared all her plans
to carry out the enslavement of our country and she
is waiting only for China, through her short-sightedness,
to fall into her trap.

(to be continued)
page_data.zh:
日本帝国主义者发明的征服中国和消灭中国人民的新方法。日本现在已经准备好所有计划来实施对我国的奴役，只等待中国因短视而落入其陷阱。

（待续）

January 6, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Sin wan Pao and other local newspapers dated December 29,
1938 (Chungking telegram) :-

"JAPAN'S PLOTS TO CONQUER THE WHOLE OF CHINA EXPOSED
BY GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK"

(Concluded from Yesterday's Translation)

If we believe that we can preserve our
existence and independence on the basis of equality
under the very maw of the tiger, then we may be mad.
Once we yield to Japan, we shall never be able to
recover our freedom or to shake off the Japanese yoke.
Japan's evil designs upon China are being exposed
to-day; these designs have been handed down year after
year by tradition and have always been in the minds
of the Japanese people. During the past few decades
Japan has suffered much loss through incompetent
statesmen and since then she has never had any far-
sighted statesmen nor have efforts ever been made to
check the activities of the Japanese militarists who
act in violation of law and discipline or to prevent
them from having a free hand in national affairs. It
is for this reason that the Japanese warlords have
become more and more aggressive in their ambitious
desires and have long intended to bring China under
their control. It is because we took up arms against
their invasion in July, 1937 that they have failed to
realize their plans to bring China to submission without
military loss. Our resistance has gradually exposed
to the world their treacherous plots and outrageous
designs. Had we failed to take up arms against their
aggression in 1937 and allowed them to extend their
acts of aggression, China would have been gradually
weakened physically and paralyzed mentally and within
five years she would have become a conquered nation.
Take, for instance, the methods Japan
employed in her annexation of Korea. On the one hand
she advocated friendly co-operation with Korea to help
the latter to acquire independence, while on the other
she employed treacherous means, such as coercion,
inducements and instigation, to bring about the
disintegration of Korea. It was by such means that
Japan succeeded in annexing Korea without incurring
any resistance from the Koreans.
Our resistance in the past 18 months
has greatly enhanced our national feelings. This
coupled with the indomitable courage and national spirit
of sacrifice of over a million of our soldiers fighting
at the front and millions of our people in the rear
has forced the enemy to discard its mask and expose
to the world its grim appearance. By so doing, not
only will China be free from the danger of being
conquered by Japan, but the world will take heed and
realize that if the aggressive acts of this outrageous
nation are unrestrained and tolerated, they might cause
a serious menace to the peace and order of the whole
page_data.zh:
1939年1月6日。下午译件。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸1938年12月29日讯（重庆电）：-

“蒋介石将军揭露日本征服全中国的阴谋”

（接昨日译文）

如果我们认为可以在虎口之下基于平等保持生存和独立，那我们就是疯了。一旦我们向日本屈服，我们将永远无法恢复自由或摆脱日本的枷锁。日本对中国的邪恶图谋今日正被揭露；这些图谋由传统年复一年地传承下来，一直存在于日本人民的脑海中。在过去几十年里，日本因政治家无能而遭受巨大损失，此后她从未有过有远见的政治家，也从未努力遏制违反法律和纪律的日本军国主义分子的活动，或防止他们在国家事务中为所欲为。正因如此，日本军阀在其野心欲望上变得愈发咄咄逼人，并长期意图将中国置于其控制之下。正是因为我们于1937年7月起武装抵抗其入侵，他们才未能实现不经军事损失就使中国屈服的计划。我们的抵抗逐渐向世界揭露了他们奸诈的阴谋和荒谬的图谋。如果我们在1937年没有武装抵抗其侵略，任由其扩展侵略行径，中国将在体力上逐渐衰弱，在精神上陷入瘫痪，并在五年内成为一个被征服的国家。
以日本吞并朝鲜时所采用的方法为例。一方面，她主张与朝鲜友好合作以帮助后者获得独立，另一方面，她采用胁迫、利诱和煽动等奸诈手段，导致朝鲜解体。日本正是通过这种手段，在未遭遇朝鲜人任何抵抗的情况下成功吞并了朝鲜。
过去18个月的抵抗极大地增强了我们的民族情感。加上前线百万将士和后方数百万民众不屈的勇气和牺牲精神，迫使敌人撕下面具，向世界暴露其狰狞面目。这样做，不仅使中国免于被日本征服的危险，也让世界警惕并认识到，如果不加约束和容忍这个荒谬国家的侵略行径，可能会对整个

January 6, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

world. The sacrifice and sufferings we have to bear
in this resistance are, of course, great, but they
are not made in vain because our nation and our country
can thus be saved from collapse and the world prevented
from being plunged into another disaster. It is for
this reason that our sacrifices and sufferings have
a very significant viewpoint. Our indomitable courage
and spirit have created for us an impregnable stronghold
for our national existence and independence.
My comrades! We must realize fully
this point and exert more efforts towards the fulfillment
of our obligations towards our nation. A general study
of Japan's plots against us has now revealed to us the
mad designs of our enemy. We are totally at a loss to
understand why the enemy could have become so devoid
of common sense and reasoning. Is it possible for a
nation that has only a population of 70,000,000 people
to conquer a country that has a history of 5,000 years,
a population of 450,000,000 people and an area of
more than 12,000,000 square miles? Can a revolutionary
government which has its own principles and understanding
be easily made to submit to the oppression of others
and forsake its mission for national salvation?
The enemy is intending to seize control
of our military affairs under pretext of joint action
against communism, to monopolize our economic resources
by means of an economic mission and to seize control
of our political as well as cultural affairs as a means
to destroy the existence of our nation under the pretext
of promoting collective co-operation in East Asia.
What a discreet and smart plan this is! The enemy has
again and again declared that inseparable and mutual
relations for political and economic as well as cultural
co-operation should be established among Japan, Manchukuo
and China. In other words, this means that the enemy
is intending to eradicate the existence and independence
of the Chinese nation and to acquire hegemony in East
Asia by political and economic as well as cultural
means.
To tell the truth, besides China, there
is no other country in East Asia that has an independent
culture. China constitutes the nucleus of East Asia.
If China is deprived of her independence and existence,
there can be no economic co-operation in East Asia.
Take, for instance, the politics in East Asia. The
politics of China alone which have as their basis
friendship, sincerity and justice can be regarded as
the leading factor in East Asia during the past 5,000
years. The Three Principles of the People of our late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen constitute the safeguard for everlasting
peace and the principal doctrine for freedom on the
basis of equality and independence. What kind of
politics has Japan? Instead of coming to her senses,
Japan intends to conquer China as a means to bring about
the reconstruction of East Asia. It seems that Japan
lacks common sense and proper understanding. If there
is no China in this world, there will be no East Asia
to say nothing of Japan.
page_data.zh:
1939年1月6日。下午译件。

世界的和平与秩序造成严重威胁。我们在抵抗中必须承受的牺牲和苦难固然巨大，但并非徒劳，因为我们的国家和民族由此得以免于崩溃，世界也得以免于陷入另一场灾难。正因如此，我们的牺牲和苦难具有非常重要的意义。我们不屈的勇气和精神为我们的民族生存和独立创造了坚不可摧的堡垒。
同志们！我们必须充分认识到这一点，并为履行对民族的义务付出更多努力。对日本针对我们的阴谋进行全面研究，现已向我们揭示了敌人的疯狂图谋。我们完全无法理解敌人为何会变得如此缺乏常识和理性。一个只有7000万人口的国家，怎么可能征服一个拥有5000年历史、4.5亿人口和超过1200万平方英里面积的国家？一个拥有自己原则和认知的革命政府，怎么可能轻易屈服于他人的压迫并放弃其救国使命？
敌人意图以联合反共为借口控制我们的军事事务，通过经济使命垄断我们的经济资源，并以促进东亚集体合作为借口控制我们的政治及文化事务，以此作为毁灭我们民族存在的手段。这是一个多么周密而狡猾的计划！敌人一再宣称，应在日、满、华之间建立政治、经济及文化合作的不可分割和相互关系。换言之，这意味着敌人意图通过政治、经济及文化手段 eradicate（消除）中华民族的生存和独立，并在东亚获取霸权。
说实话，除了中国，东亚没有其他拥有独立文化的国家。中国构成东亚的核心。如果中国失去其独立和存在，东亚就不可能有经济合作。以东亚政治为例。在过去5000年里，唯有以友谊、真诚和正义为基础的中国政治，才能被视为东亚的主导因素。我们已故孙中山博士的三民主义构成了永久和平的保障，以及基于平等和独立的自由的主要学说。日本有什么样的政治？日本非但没有清醒过来，反而意图通过征服中国来实现东亚的重建。日本似乎缺乏常识和正确的理解。如果这个世界上没有中国，也就没有东亚，更不用说日本了。

page_data.en:
January 6, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

The activities of the Japanese warlords
in China which aim at the subjugation of this country
can only hasten the collapse of Japan, because we have
already established our foundation for national revival
during the past 18 months of our resistance. We fear
no difficulties nor obstacles. It was through so much
painstaking effort and strenuous labour on the part of
the Japanese people during the regime of the Emperor
Meiji that Japan became the strong nation that she is
at present. But now everything is in the hands of the
young militarists. They have wasted vainly Japan's
national strength and shaken her national foundation.
It is indeed a pity to see Japan gradually collapse.
In the eyes of these militarists, there is no China nor
world; there is no discipline nor law. Unless efforts
are made to check such activities, Japan will meet with
serious danger. Though we harbour a great hatred against
the Japanese militarists, yet in view of the fact that
Japan is our neighbour and that the Japanese people are of
the same race as we are We feel pity for them.

My comrades, the enemy militarists have
now reached the climax of their outrageous acts. They
have now only two courses to take: either to force us
to submission by means of outrageous and harsh demands
or to seize special rights in this country by means of
quick and easy methods. They take it for granted that
the world can be easily deceived and that might is right.

The various points contained in Konoye's
statement aim at (1) the closing of the door of China
and the violation of the Nine-Power Treaty under the
pretext of the establishment of a new order in East Asia,
(2) the eradication of European and American influences
from the Far East by means of collective co-operation
in East Asia and (3) the revival of Japan's 21 demands
under the pretext of stationing troops in North China
and the demarcation of Inner Mongolia as a special area
for anti-communist purposes. To put it briefly, the
so-called new order in East Asia and the various other
slogans advocated by Prince Konoye are only intended to
induce China to destroy on her own initiative the open
door principle for equal opportunity and to impair the
League Covenant, the Nine-Power Pact, the Sino-Soviet
Non-Aggression Pact, and other international treaties.
Japan not only intends to bind us and control our
economic resources, but desires China to help her to
secure hegemony in East Asia and to realize her object
for control of the whole world, contrary to justice
and right. How can China, a nation which has as her
national foundation the maintenance of justice and right
in the past 5,000 years, be willing to forsake her
original status because of Japanese oppression? It will
be remembered that when Tanaka came to Shanghai in the
1st Year (1912) of the Chinese Republic and had a
conversation with our late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, he said that
we should shake off all relations with foreign nations
and establish a new status in East Asia. To this, the
late Dr. Sun Yat-sen asked: "Will not this violate the
page_data.zh:
1939年1月6日。下午译件。

日本军阀在中国旨在征服本国的活动，只会加速日本的崩溃，因为我们在过去18个月的抗战中已经奠定了民族复兴的基础。我们不畏任何困难与障碍。日本之所以成为如今的强国，是得益于明治天皇统治时期日本人民付出的巨大心血和辛勤劳动。但现在，一切大权都落入年轻军国主义者手中。他们白白浪费了日本的国力，动摇了其国家根基。眼见日本逐渐走向崩溃，实令人惋惜。在这些军国主义者眼中，没有中国，也没有世界；没有纪律，也没有法律。若不设法遏制此类活动，日本将面临严重危险。尽管我们对日本军国主义者怀有极大仇恨，但鉴于日本是我国邻邦，且日本人民与我们同种同源，我们对其感到怜悯。

同胞们，敌方军国主义者的暴行现已达到顶峰。他们现在只有两条路可走：要么通过 outrageous 和苛刻的要求迫使我们屈服，要么通过快捷简便的手段攫取在华特权。他们理所当然地认为世界容易被欺骗，且强权即公理。

近卫声明中的各点旨在：（1）以建立东亚新秩序为借口，关闭中国大门并违反《九国公约》；（2）通过东亚集体合作，消除欧美在远东的影响；以及（3）以在华北驻军及划定内蒙古为防共特区为借口，复活日本的“二十一条”。简而言之，近卫亲王所倡导的所谓“东亚新秩序”及其他各种口号，仅意在诱使中国主动破坏机会均等的门户开放原则，并损害《国际联盟盟约》、《九国公约》、《中苏互不侵犯条约》及其他国际条约。日本不仅意图束缚我们并控制我们的经济资源，还希望中国帮助其确立在东亚的霸权，并实现其违背正义与公理的控制全世界的目标。中国作为一个五千年来以维护正义与公理为立国基础的民族，怎会因日本的压迫而愿意放弃其原有地位？值得回忆的是，当田中义一于民国元年（1912年）来到上海并与已故孙中山博士会谈时，他说我们应该切断与外国的一切关系，在东亚建立新地位。对此，已故孙中山博士问道：“这难道不会违反

page_data.en:
international treaties?", whereupon Tanaka replied:
"To tear international treaties and to abolish all
unequal relations will only be advantageous to China."
This was, however, rejected by our late Dr. Sun who
said: "We should bring about the abolition of unequal
treaties through legitimate and proper procedure. We
would not do such a thing if not through proper channels,
even though it might be beneficial to China."
This is the spirit of China and of the
Three Principles of the People. We rely on this spirit
in our resistance against all coercion and invasion,
for the restoration of order in East Asia and for the
establishment of everlasting peace in the world.
In short, this war on the part of Japan
is but a desperate move that will hasten the collapse
of her moral discipline and character, but on the part
of China it is a righteous movement. As a matter of
fact, all the nations in the world should adopt sanctions
against aggressors so as to fulfill their obligations
under international treaties. Unfortunately, however,
they have remained indifferent. It is for this reason
that we have started the present war of resistance, which
aims to bring about the realization of our national
revolutionary object, to secure independence and freedom,
to maintain justice, to uphold the sanctity of treaties
and to restore peace and order. The present war of
resistance can be regarded as a struggle between right
and wrong, justice and might and treaty-observers and
breakers. So long as we remain firm in our determination
and spirit and continue our resistance with undaunted
spirit and courage, final victory will be ours.

国际条约吗？”田中回答说：“废除国际条约并取消一切不平等关系，只对中国有利。”然而，这一建议被已故孙中山博士拒绝，他说：“我们应该通过合法和正当的程序来废除不平等条约。即使这样做可能对中国有利，如果不通过正当渠道，我们也不会这样做。”

这就是中国与三民主义的精神。我们依靠这种精神抵抗一切胁迫与侵略，以恢复东亚秩序并建立世界永久和平。

总之，日本发动的这场战争不过是加速其道德纪律与品格崩溃的绝望之举，而对中国而言，这是一场正义的运动。事实上，世界各国都应制裁侵略者，以履行其在国际条约下的义务。然而不幸的是，各国一直漠不关心。正因如此，我们开始了目前的抗战，旨在实现我们的国民革命目标，确保独立与自由，维护正义， uphold 条约的神圣性，并恢复和平与秩序。目前的抗战可被视为正与邪、正义与强权、守约者与毁约者之间的斗争。只要我们坚定决心与精神，以大无畏的精神和勇气继续抵抗，最终胜利必将属于我们。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JUL 7 1938

Wang's Office Here
Inside Fortress
Confiscated Property on
Yu Yuen Road Being
"Fortified"

Some 100 masons and carpenters are busily engaged day and night in converting the recently confiscated residence of M. Wang Pa-chun, former Minister of Communications and brother-in-law of the present Minister of War in Chungking, into a formidable fortress, with pill-boxes at regular intervals and large iron spokes being placed in such a manner as to make the premises impregnable.

The building, which reputedly cost $1,000,000 to construct some three or four years ago, is situated in the centre of a large garden, on Yu Yuen Road immediately East of the Hollywood Garden and, whilst two of the pill-boxes which face Yu Yuen Road, may be seen from the street, the building itself lies deep inside. A "North-China Daily News" reporter walked into alleyway 1136 and viewed the Gothic-style palatial residence through solid steel gates, which had been opened to permit the arrival of building materials.

All windows are barred and further protected by strong steel-netting, whilst some of the larger windows have been given additional protection by the emplacement of heavy steel plates. The watchman's hut next to the large gate, is being re-inforced with cement from the inside whilst all around the workmen were busy, rushing their job through as fast as possible.

Enquiries made in the vicinity elicited nothing with regard to the purpose to which this building is to be put but it was subsequently learned that many plans had been studied by the Japanese authorities since they confiscated the premises some three months ago. The original idea was to convert it into a court house but this was found impracticable whereupon the possibilities of making this palace, the future Shanghai residence of Mr. Wang Ching-wei was gone into, although it was soon discarded in view of the proximity of Hollywood Gardens from where an attempt on the statesman could easily be made.

The gambling-den operators then tried to rent the premises but were not successful in their attempt, and, whilst no confirmation of this report could be obtained, it was reliably learned that Mr. Wang Ching-wei's offices will move into this fortress once it is completed whilst he will reside in the French Concession when in Shanghai.

The constructional work is being supervised by armed plain-clothes members of the Japanese Special Service Corps and trespassers are not admitted. When an attempt was made to take a photograph from outside the gate, a vehement "No" was all the Japanese officials said.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，

1938年7月7日

汪精卫办事处设于此处
堡垒内部
愚园路没收房产正在
“加固”

大约100名泥瓦匠和木匠日夜忙碌，将前交通部长、现任重庆战争部长姻兄弟王伯群先生最近被没收的住宅改造成一座坚固的堡垒，每隔一段距离设有碉堡，并安装大型铁辐条，以使该处固若金汤。

据称，这座建筑建于三四年前，耗资100万美元，位于一个大花园的中心，在好莱坞花园（Hollywood Garden）以东的愚园路上。虽然从街上可以看到面向愚园路的两座碉堡，但建筑物本身深藏在内。一名《字林西报》记者走进1136弄，透过实心钢门观看了这座哥特式风格的宫殿式住宅，钢门打开是为了让建筑材料进入。

所有窗户都装有栏杆，并进一步用坚固的钢丝网保护，而一些较大的窗户则通过安置厚重的钢板得到了额外保护。大门旁边的门卫室正从内部用水泥加固，周围的工人们都在忙碌，尽可能快地赶工。

在附近进行的询问并未获悉该建筑用途的任何信息，但后来得知，自日本当局三个月前没收该房产以来，已研究了许多计划。最初的想法是将其改为法院，但发现不可行；随后研究了将该宫殿作为汪精卫先生未来上海寓所的可能性，但由于靠近好莱坞花园，容易从此处对这位政治家发动袭击，该方案很快被放弃。

赌场经营者随后试图租赁该处，但未成功。虽然无法证实此报道，但有可靠消息得知，一旦堡垒完工，汪精卫先生的办事处将迁入此处，而他在上海期间将居住在法租界。

施工工作由日本特务机关的武装便衣人员监督，闲杂人等不得入内。当有人试图从门外拍照时，日本官员只严厉地说了一声“不”。

0751
1939年4月11日

汪精卫
据称在上海

中文报纸报道
其从南方秘密抵达

引用虹口抵达人士消息的中文报纸报道称，汪精卫已秘密抵达上海。据说他住在虹口，但也承认难以获得证实。不过，有人指出，汪先生很可能已抵达此处，因为他的几名下属在此地活动频繁。

最近的报道显示，汪先生的下属除了在香港进行宣传工作外，许多擅长写作的人已来到上海出版一本杂志。据说该杂志名为《抗议》（Protest），刊登了阐述汪先生和平提议的文章。

上海的几个中国公共团体已致电重庆，请求逮捕汪先生。据报道，最新的请愿书是由上海码头苦力工会发出的。

CHINA PRESS.

APR 1 1 1939

Wang Said
Setting Up
Offices Here

Chou Fu-hai Held Slated
To Head Pro-Nippon
Publication

Chief lieutenants of Wang Ching-wei, ousted Kuomintang official, have set up an office in Shanghai to conduct propaganda for their pro-Japanese cause, a Chinese report said last night.

It was indicated that the first task of Wang's headquarters here will be the publication of a Chinese daily. Thus far, the report said, no printing firm in Shanghai had yet agreed to participate in the undertaking.

Three of Wang's assistants were said to have made frequent trips to Shanghai, among them being Lin Pei-sheng, editor of Wang's newspaper, in Hongkong, and Mei Shi-ping, one of Wang's chief advisers.

Another aim of Wang's headquarters here is to rally the aid of bandits in the guerilla areas, the report stated.

Meanwhile, a well-informed Chinese source asserted that Wang's publicity man, Chou Fu-hai, had taken up residence in Hongkew ever since his chief's flight to Hanoi. Chou was said to be living in Broadway Mansions.

Should Wang be successful in establishing a newspaper here, the report added, Chou will direct its publication from across the creek.

（批：M. Pan / last n/u）
（批：Fink）

《大美晚报》。

1939年4月11日

据称汪精卫
在此设立
办事处

周佛海被拘
拟主持亲日
出版物

昨晚有中文报道说，被罢免的国民党官员汪精卫的主要副手已在上海设立办事处，为其亲日事业进行宣传。

报道指出，汪精卫在此处的总部首要任务是出版一份中文日报。报道说，到目前为止，上海尚无印刷公司同意参与此项事业。

据说汪精卫的三名助手频繁往返上海，其中包括汪精卫在香港的报纸编辑林柏生，以及汪精卫的主要顾问之一梅思平。

报道还称，汪精卫在此处总部的另一个目标是集结游击区匪帮的援助。

与此同时，一位消息灵通的中方人士声称，自汪精卫的主子逃往河内以来，汪的宣传人员周佛海一直居住在虹口。据说周佛海住在百老汇大厦。

报道补充说，如果汪精卫成功在此创办报纸，周佛海将在苏州河对岸指导其出版工作。

（批注：潘先生 / 最后未核实）
（批注：芬克）

Mr. Wang Ching-wei, the self-exiled

《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年4月14日

汪精卫先生在何处？
其在上海的报道
被认为不属实

虽然仍缺乏关于国民党自我流放的副书记长汪精卫先生身处上海的证实，但消息灵通的中国圈子表示，现在可以肯定的是，他的许多亲密追随者，包括前国民党宣传部长周佛海先生，一直在上海进行政治活动。

这些同一圈子的人士对汪先生确实已来上海表示怀疑，他们认为他目前可能在香港或广州的说法更有可能。

同时，另有报道说，周先生及其同事目前正在组织一份报纸，办事处将设在伯基尔路（Burkill Road）某处。进一步报道说，该报名称为《远东日报》（Far Eastern Daily News），将成为汪精卫先生的官方喉舌，借此表达他对时事的个人观点。

兰督察，
已阅

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
03845
APR 1 3 1939

Wang Charged With
Falsifying Minutes
Of Defense Council

Wu Tze-hui, Veteran
Statesman, Issues
Strong Letter

CHUNGKING, Apr. 12.—(Reu-
ters).—The charge that many al-
leged passages from minutes of
secret meetings of the National
Defense Council, made public in a
recent statement by Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, deposed President of the
Executive Yuan, did not appear in
the official records and were pure
inventions, was made today by Mr.
Wu Tze-hui, the celebrated Chinese
"elder statesman," in an open letter
to Mr. Wang.

Mr. Wu dealt at length with the
peace overtures made through the
former German Ambassador to
China, Dr. Trautmann, and declar-
ed that many of the "revelations"
made by Mr. Wang Ching-wei were
false.

In referring to the peace negotia-
tions, he declared, Mr. Wang had
tried to disguise the fact that Japan
had asked Germany to talk peace
with China.

Mr. Wu's letter said:—
"You alleged that when Dr.
Trautmann called on the Chinese
Foreign Minister, Mr. Wang Chung-
hui, he said that when the German
Ambassador in Tokyo saw the
Japanese Foreign Minister and the
Japanese Minister of War, he asked
them if Japan wanted to liquidate
the present situation, and, if so,
under what conditions.

"Never Appeared"

"Such a passage never appeared
in the official records. This is your
attempt to disguise the fact that
Japan had asked Germany to talk
peace.

"The passage that details the
anti-Japanese question also never
appeared in the official records.

"Your remarks concerning the
statements by General Tang Sen-
chi, General Pai Chung-hsi, Vice-
Minister Hsu Mo and General Ku
Chu-tung could not be found in the
official records.

"You quoted Dr. Trautmann as
declaring: 'China, in her resistance
against Japan, has amply demons-
trated her spirit of resistance. This
is the time for the termination of
hostilities. In the Great War,
there were several good opportuni-
ties for peace, but Germany, con-
fident of her own strength, refused
peace until, at Versailles, she was
compelled to accept any terms
dictated by others. I believe that
the Japanese terms are not impos-
sible of acceptance.' This passage
also never appeared in the official
records."
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。
03845
1939年4月13日

汪被指控
伪造国防最高会议
会议记录

资深政治家
吴稚晖发表
措辞严厉之信函

重庆，4月12日.—（路透
社）.—今日，中国著名“元老”
吴稚晖先生在一封致汪精卫的
公开信中指出，已被罢免的行
政院院长汪精卫先生在近期发
表的声明中公布的所谓国法国
防最高会议秘密会议记录中的
许多段落，并未出现在官方记
录中，纯属捏造。

吴先生详细论述了通过前德
国驻华大使陶德曼博士（Dr.
Trautmann）进行的和平试探，
并宣称汪精卫先生所作的许多
“揭露”均为虚假。

在提及和平谈判时，他宣
称，汪试图掩盖日本曾要求德
国与中国进行和平谈判这一事
实。

吴先生的信中说：—
“你声称，当陶德曼博士拜
会中国外交部长王宠惠先生
时，他说，德国驻东京大使在
会见日本外务大臣和陆军大臣
时，询问他们日本是否希望了
结当前局势，如果是，条件如
何。

‘从未出现’

“此类段落从未出现在官方
记录中。这是你试图掩盖日本
曾要求德国进行和平谈判这一
事实。

“详述反日问题的段落也从未
出现在官方记录中。

“你关于唐生智将军、白崇
禧将军、次长徐谟和顾祝同将
军言论的内容，在官方记录中
无法找到。

“你引用陶德曼博士的话
称：‘中国在抵抗日本的过程中，
已充分展示了其抵抗精神。现
在是终止敌对行动的时候了。
在大战期间，曾有数次良好的
和平机会，但德国因自信其力
量，拒绝和平，直到在凡尔赛
被迫接受他人强加的任何条
款。我认为日本的条款并非不
可接受。’此段也未出现在官
方记录中。”

page_data.en:
03846

Divergences Found

"We ought to specially emphasize
this point, for otherwise Dr. Traut-
mann would be held responsible for
such statements by the German
Government. The integrity of the
Chinese Foreign Office would also
be affected. Numerous other such
divergences from the documents
have been made.
"You say that the Communists
habitually create disturbances. So
far, we have not seen any distur-
bances created by the Communists,
but we have seen you publicly sur-
render to the enemy.
"I would like to mention one
example. In 1934, when you were
Foreign Minister and concurrently
President of the Executive Yuan, as
soon as Japan demanded the dis-
missal of Mr. Sung Cheh-yuan, then
Governor of Chahar, you imme-
diately ordered his dismissal.
"Thus, within 24 hours, you gave
Chahar to Japan. You are not
different from Dr. Hacha, the last
President of Czechoslovakia."

发现差异

“我们应特别强调这一点，否
则陶德曼博士将因这些言论而

“你说共产党人惯于制造骚

“我想举一个例子。1934年，

“因此，你在24小时内便将

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 3 1939
S. S. REGISTRY
AL POLICE
Peace Urgently Needed, S. B. D.
Says Wang Ching-wei In
His Latest Declaration

Interesting Revelations Of Mediatary Efforts By
Dr. Oscar Trautmann, Then German Ambassador;
Searching Questions Put by Mr. Wang

CO-EXISTENCE VITAL FOR BOTH LANDS;
THE DANGER OF DESTRUCTION

HONGKONG, April 1.—Co-operation with Japan was the
“indispensable way” for China to maintain her existence and
independence and bring about stability in East Asia, instead of
following the “common road to destruction” by carrying on
hostilities, Mr. Wang Ching-wei, former Deputy General
Executive of the Kuomintang, declared in a new peace
statement issued here last night.

There could be no doubt, he said, that Japan and China
must follow the same road to co-existence and co-prosperity.

The former Kuomintang execu-
tive said he could not agree with
those who said China was able to
attain unity only by resistance and
that if she made peace the country
would again be reduced to a state
of disunity.

“If resistance is for the sake of
the existence and independence of
the State, then it is quite a different
question,” he declared; “but if
resistance is resorted to as a means
of bringing about internal unity,
then I am absolutely against it.”

If China and Japan co-operated
with each other for peace they
would certainly be able to bring
about “everlasting stability in East
Asia, and if not they will both suf-
fer damage and both come to
collapse,” Mr. Wang stated.

Chiang Was Ready To Accept
His statement disclosed that Gen-
eral Chiang Kai-shek and high
military officers of the Kuomintang
had expressed their willingness to
accept peace terms offered by Dr.
Oscar Trautmann, then German
Ambassador to China, on November
28 and 29, 1937.

General Chiang was willing to
have Germany act as intermediary
and Dr. Trautmann regarded his
interview with the Generalissimo
as a success, Mr. Wang’s statement
revealed.

Comparing the peace terms
advanced by Dr. Trautmann in 1937
with the statement made by Prince
Ayamaro Konoye when he was
Premier of Japan on December 22,
1938, Mr. Wang expressed wonder
as to why the terms of 1937, which
he said were more stringent than
the views contained in Prince
Konoye’s statement, were accepted
by General Chiang as a basis for
negotiation, while the Prince
Konoye statement was not so
regarded.

Mr. Wang pointed out that at
the time Dr. Trautmann approach-
ed General Chiang and high mili-
tary officers in 1937, China’s mili-
tary situation was not as unfavour-
able as when Prince Konye’s state-
ment was made. Nanking, Hankow
and numerous other cities had
fallen to the Japanese in the
intervening year, he recalled.

Members of the Supreme National
Defence Conference of the
Kuomintang had expressed their
approval of negotiations for peace
at the time of Dr. Trautmann’s
intervention, Mr. Wang’s statement
said, citing a report of Mr. Hsu
Mo, Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs
in the Kuomintang Government.

Aim Of The State
The aim of the State was its
existence and independence, and
either peace or war was “nothing
but a means to that end,” Mr.
Wang declared.

“Whether making peace deserves
approval depends on the conditions
of peace,” he stated. “If they are
detrimental to the existence and
independence of the State, peace
should not be made; if they are
otherwise, peace should be made.”

Mr. Wang declared that China
should follow an independent
diplomatic policy and decide for
herself whether she should make
peace, disregarding the attitude of
other countries.

Mr. Wang revealed that in the
middle of February, the Chungking
regime sent a member of the
Central Executive Council to him
and tried to persuade him to go
abroad, offering to grant him a
passport.

In a reply to the Chungking
regime, Mr. Wang stated that he
did not wish to leave the country.

What Tseng Chung-Ming Said
The statement quoted Dr. Tseng
Chung-ming, colleague of Mr.
Wang, slain by Chinese gunmen
recently, as having said just before
his death: “The affairs of the
State are in the hands of Mr.
Wang and the affairs of my family
are in the hands of my wife. I have
no cause to worry about either.”

“Mr. Tseng Chung-ming died for
the State and his stand towards the
conduct of its affairs,” Mr. Wang’s
statement continued. “His views on
the affairs of the State are identical
with mine and, naturally, the result
of his contentions would be
similar to mine. He died, deeply
concerned over our cause. If
Providence had spared him a few
more minutes I could have con-
soled him and assured him that
we shared a common belief. I am
prepared to exert myself to the
utmost to realize this cause upon
which the existence of the nation
and the race is staked.

A Cry For Peace
“I have already urged peace in
my statement of December 28 last
year. That is not only my own
opinion, but it is a cry born out
of the state of the nation. This
attitude was arrived at collectively
after discussions in the supreme
councils of the State. There are
countless facts which prove my
contention but I will point out
only two to support my theory.

“First, I would like to quote
from a report delivered by Mr.

汪精卫在其最新声明中
称亟需和平

有趣地揭露了时任德国大使奥斯卡·陶德曼博士的调停努力；
汪先生提出尖锐问题

两国共存至关重要；
毁灭的危险

香港，4月1日.—国民党前副
总裁汪精卫昨晚在此间发表新
的和平声明，宣称与日本合作
是中国维持生存与独立、实现
东亚稳定的“不可或缺之道”，
而非通过继续敌对行动走上“共
同毁灭之路”。

他说，毫无疑问，日本和中
国必须走共存共荣的同一条道
路。

这位国民党前执行委员表示，
他不能同意那些认为中国只有
通过抵抗才能实现统一、如果
讲和国家将再次陷入分裂状态
的说法。

“如果抵抗是为了国家的生存
和独立，那就是另一回事，”他
宣称；“但如果将抵抗作为实现
内部统一的手段，那我绝对反
对。”

汪先生 stated，如果中日为
和平而相互合作，肯定能够实
现“东亚的永久稳定”，否则双
方都将遭受损害并走向崩溃。

蒋介石曾准备接受
他的声明披露，蒋介石将军和
国民党高级军官曾表示愿意接
受时任德国驻华大使奥斯卡·陶
德曼博士于1937年11月28日和
29日提出的和平条款。

汪的声明透露，蒋将军愿意
由德国充当调停人，陶德曼博
士认为他与委员长的会谈取得
了成功。

汪先生将陶德曼博士1937年
提出的和平条款与日本首相近
卫文麿亲王1938年12月22日发
表的声明进行了比较，并对
1937年的条款（他称这些条款
比近卫亲王声明中的观点更为
苛刻）被蒋将军接受为谈判基
础，而近卫亲王的声明却未获
如此对待表示不解。

汪先生指出，1937年陶德曼
接触蒋将军和高级军官时，中
国的军事形势并不像近卫亲王
发表声明时那样不利。他回顾
说，在这一年间，南京、汉口
和许多其他城市已落入日军之
手。

汪先生的声明称，在陶德曼
介入时，国民党国防最高会议
成员曾表示赞成和平谈判，并
援引了国民党政府外交部次长
徐谟先生的报告。

国家目标
汪先生宣称，国家的目标是
其生存和独立，和平或战争只
不过是“实现这一目标的手段”。

“讲和是否值得赞同取决于和
平条件，”他 stated。“如果条件
损害国家的生存和独立，就不
应讲和；否则，就应讲和。”

汪先生宣称，中国应奉行独
立的外交政策，自行决定是否
讲和，而不顾及其他国家的态
度。

汪先生透露，2月中旬，重庆
政权派遣一名中央执行委员前
来见他，试图说服他出国，并
表示愿向他颁发护照。

汪先生在回复重庆政权时表
示，他不希望离开国家。

曾仲明所言
声明引用汪先生的同事、近
期被中国枪手杀害的曾仲明博
士在临终前的话：“国事交由汪
先生处理，家事交由我妻子处
理。我对此二者均无需担忧。”

“曾仲明先生为国家及其事务
的处理方式而死，”汪先生的声
明继续说道。“他对国事的看法
与我相同，自然，他主张的结
果也会与我相似。他去世时，
对我们的事业深感关切。如果
上天能多留他几分钟，我本可
以安慰他并向他保证我们拥有
共同的信念。我准备竭尽全力
去实现这一关乎民族与国家存
亡的事业。

和平的呼声
“我在去年12月28日的声明
中已呼吁和平。这不仅是我个
人的意见，也是源于国家状况
的呼声。这种态度是在国家最
高理事会讨论后集体达成的。
有无数事实可以证明我的主张，
但我仅指出两点以支持我的理
论。

“首先，我想引用徐谟先生

的报告，徐谟系国民党政府外
交部次长，该报告发表于1937
年12月6日上午9时在汉口中国
银行大楼举行的国防最高会议
常务委员会第54次会议上。出
席会议的有徐谟先生、孔祥熙
博士、何应钦将军、于右任将
军、朱家骅先生、陈立夫先生、
陈果夫先生、陈布雷先生等，
由我本人主持，张群先生任副
主席，曾仲明博士任首席秘书。”

解释和平条件
据汪先生称，在该报告中，
徐谟列举并解释了时任德国驻
华大使奥斯卡·陶德曼博士根据
柏林的指示，于1937年11月28
日和29日向行政院院长孔祥熙
博士提出的和平条件。

声明称，陶德曼博士的和平
提议是日本政府在东京向德国
特使提出的，作为缔结和平的
条件，以便转达给中国最高当
局。

汪先生在声明中引用徐谟列
举的条件如下：
“1.—内蒙古自治；
“2.—扩大日军在华北的驻
兵区域，但华北的行政权仍归
中央政府所有；
“日本希望不任命反日人士担
任华北最高领导人。如果现在
结束冲突，上述条件是可以接
受的；但如果在华北建立新政
权，则应允许其继续存在。如
果现在结束冲突，日本无意在
华北建立新政权。日本准备继
续进行目前正在进行的关于开
发华北矿产的谈判，以达成结
论；

上海问题
“3.—扩大上海非军事区。日
本政府尚未明确扩大的范围或
实施方法，但不会改变上海的
行政管理；
“4.—关于反日问题，希望按
照川越茂大使和张群将军（中
国外交部长）商定的路线解决。
细节仅是技术问题。
“5. — 反共。日本希望中国
采取某些措施来处理这一问题；
“6.—修订关税税则；
“7.—尊重外国人在中国的既
得权利。
“当陶德曼大使表示希望会见
行政院院长孔博士、外交部长
汪先生和蒋将军时，随即发出
了以此为目的的电报。蒋将军
立即回复称他愿意见陶德曼博
士。”

page_data.en:
Dr. Trautmann's Views
"I accompanied Dr. Trautmann to Nanking," Mr. Wang reported Mr. Hsu as having stated.
"During the course of the trip I had the opportunity for an intimate talk with Dr. Trautmann. He maintained that China had fully shown her fighting spirit in past hostilities, and it was about time for her to bring the conflict to an end. Dr. Trautmann cited Germany's example during the Great War. In spite of many occasions to talk peace, over-estimating her own power, Germany refused to make peace terms until she was forced to accept proposals by the victorious Powers in the Versailles Treaty.
"Dr. Trautmann also quoted Reichsfuehrer Hitler's statement that Japan's peace conditions were not so stringent, adding that he hoped China would consider the proposals then being made by the Japanese Government.
"Dr. Trautmann and I arrived at Nanking on December 2 and I immediately conferred with General Chiang Kai-shek, who said, after reflecting at length, that high military officials then in Nanking should be consulted.
"When I went to see General Chiang at 4 o'clock that afternoon for the second time that day General Ku Chu-tung, General Pai Chung-hsi, Kwangsi leader; General Tang Sheng-chih (member of the standing committee of the Military Affairs Council); General Hsu Yung-chang (former member of the Peking Political Committee), and others were assembled around General Chiang.

General's Questions
"Upon my reporting Dr. Trautmann's mission in coming to Nanking these military leaders asked me questions as to whether the stated peace conditions had any collateral conditions and whether they provided for limitations on Chinese armaments.
"To these I answered that, according to what Dr. Trautmann stated, these conditions were shown in their entirety and had no collateral conditions.
"General Chiang, in consulting the officers present as to whether or not an armistice should be concluded, first asked General Tang Sheng-chih, who was unable to reply at once. General Pai Chung-shih was asked for his views, whereupon General Pai said: "If these are the only conditions what are we fighting for?" I said, "The conditions presented by the German Ambassador are only these few conditions."
"General Chiang then asked General Hsu Yung-chang what his views were. General Hsu said: "If these are the conditions, we should accept them."
"General Ku Chu-tung, questioned, said, "We should agree."
"General Chiang again asked General Tang, who agreed with the majority.
"General Chiang then said that the peace proposals, as made through Germany, should not be rejected, as the conditions did not subjugate China, and that it was necessary to keep the North China regime alive.

Danger Of Procrastination
"At 5 o'clock the same afternoon General Chiang and Dr. Trautmann had a conversation at which I interpreted. Dr. Trautmann asked General Chiang just what he had previously asked Dr. Wang Chung-hui and Dr. H. H. Kung at Hankow, only adding that if the Kuomintang were to continue hostilities without accepting the present proposals, the peace conditions which might be made by Japan in the future would be far more exacting and rigorous than those now presented.
page_data.zh:
陶德曼博士的观点
“我陪同陶德曼博士前往南京，”汪先生报告说，徐先生曾如此陈述。
“在旅途中，我有机会与陶德曼博士进行了一次深入交谈。他坚持认为，中国在过去的敌对行动中已充分展现了其战斗精神，现在是结束冲突的时候了。陶德曼博士引用了大战期间德国的例子。尽管有许多和谈的机会，但德国因高估自身实力，拒绝接受和平条款，直到被迫接受战胜国在《凡尔赛条约》中提出的条件。
“陶德曼博士还引用了元首希特勒的声明，称日本的和平条件并不那么苛刻，并补充说，他希望中国考虑日本政府当时提出的建议。
“陶德曼博士和我于12月2日抵达南京，我随即与蒋介石将军会晤，蒋将军在经过长时间深思后表示，应咨询当时在南京的高级军事官员。
“当天下午4点，我第二次去见蒋将军时，顾祝同将军、广西领袖白崇禧将军、唐生智将军（军事委员会常务委员）、徐永昌将军（前北平政治委员会委员）等人正聚集在蒋将军周围。

将军们的提问
“当我汇报陶德曼博士来南京的使命时，这些军事领导人向我提问，询问所述的和平条件是否有任何附带条件，以及是否规定了对中国军备的限制。
“对此我回答说，据陶德曼博士所述，这些条件已完整列出，没有任何附带条件。
“蒋将军在征询在场军官关于是否应缔结停战协定的意见时，首先询问唐生智将军，唐未能立即答复。随后征求白崇禧将军的意见，白将军说：‘如果只有这些条件，那我们打仗是为了什么？’我说：‘德国大使提出的条件仅有这几条。’
“接着，蒋将军询问徐永昌将军的看法。徐将军说：‘如果是这些条件，我们应该接受。’
“被问及的顾祝同将军说：‘我们应该同意。’
“蒋将军再次询问唐将军，唐表示赞同多数人的意见。
“蒋将军随后表示，不应拒绝通过德国提出的和平建议，因为这些条件并未使中国屈服，且有必要维持华北政权的存在。

拖延的危险
“同日下午5时，蒋将军与陶德曼博士进行了谈话，由我担任翻译。陶德曼博士向蒋将军提出了他此前在汉口向汪精卫博士和孔祥熙博士提出的相同问题，只是补充说，如果国民党不接受目前的建议而继续敌对行动，日本未来可能提出的和平条件将比现在提出的条件苛刻和严厉得多。

page_data.en:
"To this statement by Dr.
Trautmann, General Chiang answer-
ed: "Although Japan cannot be
trusted. Japan blithely breaks
treaties and her assurances cannot
be counted upon, China appreciates
the good offices offered by Ger-
many, with whom she is on good
terms. She also appreciates the
good faith of Germany. In negotiat-
ing peace upon these conditions,
however, I would like to have
Your Excellency kindly report to
Berlin on two points, namely, that
Germany is requested to act as
arbitrator throughout the Sino-
Japanese negotiations and that the
administration of North China
should be strictly maintained. China
is willing to enter into peace
negotiations within the above con-
ditions, which are tantamount to
the fact that Japan should not
assume the attitude of a victorious
Power, and that her peace proposals
should not be made in the form
of an ultimatum."

Reminder On Realities
"In reply to these remarks, Mr.
Trautmann asked to be permitted
to say that, in the face of realities,
the Chinese Government had better
not make demands to which it was
not fully entitled.
"General Chiang Kai-shek then
requested Dr. Trautmann to see if
Germany would also use its good
offices to advise Japan to conclude
peace. Dr. Trautmann promised to
convey the two points brought up
by General Chiang to the Berlin
Government. Reichsfuehrer Hitler
also wanted to make peace pro-
posals to Japan and China equally,
Dr. Trautmann stated.
"General Chiang further said
to Dr. Trautmann, "If Japan was
to pose as a victorious nation and
contend that China had already
accepted Japan's peace proposals,
then China would be unable to
resume peace talks." Concluding
his conversation with General
Chiang, Dr. Trautmann expressed
the opinion to me that it was very
successful.

Not An Ultimatum
"Dr. Trautmann also told Gen-
eral Chiang at Nanking that these
conditions were not an ultimatum.
The German Ambassador dispatch-
ed a cable to Berlin via Tokyo
from the boat on his return voyage,
but subsequent developments were
not yet known, as a reply has not
been received by Dr. Trautmann
since then,' Mr. Hsu's report con-
cluded.
"On December 28 last year, in a
letter addressed to the Supreme
National Defence Conference I
(Mr. Wang Chnig-wei) stated as
follows: 'The conditions proposed
by Japan as presented by Dr.
Trautmann in his interview with
General Chiang Kai-shek at the
beginning of December last year,
when Nanking had not yet fallen,
were not so well defined as those
now before us, and rather more
stringent, and yet General Chiang
Kai-shek, in consideration of the
ultimate trend of the situation,
agreed to make those conditions the
basis of negotiations for peace.
"As is seen in the above, it is
quite clear that what I have thus
stated is very concrete.
"If asked for more evidence, I
shall be able to list one hundred
or one thousand more facts; but as
these things are not yet of the past,
it is necessary to keep them secret
page_data.zh:
“针对陶德曼博士的这一陈述，蒋将军回答说：‘虽然日本不可信任，日本随意撕毁条约，其保证不可靠，但中国感激德国提供的斡旋，中国与德国关系良好。中国也感激德国的诚意。然而，在基于这些条件进行和谈时，我希望阁下向柏林报告两点，即请求德国在整个中日谈判过程中担任仲裁人，并严格维持华北的行政管辖。中国愿意在上述条件下进入和平谈判，这相当于日本不应采取战胜国的姿态，其和平提议也不应以最后通牒的形式提出。’

现实提醒
“作为对这些言论的回应，陶德曼先生请求允许他说，面对现实，中国政府最好不要提出其无权 fully 享有的要求。
“随后，蒋介石将军请求陶德曼博士看看德国是否也能利用其斡旋，劝告日本达成和平。陶德曼博士承诺将蒋将军提出的两点转达给柏林政府。陶德曼博士 stated，元首希特勒也希望向日本和中国同等地提出和平建议。
“蒋将军进一步对陶德曼博士说：‘如果日本摆出战胜国的姿态，并声称中国已经接受了日本的和平提议，那么中国将无法恢复和谈。’在与蒋将军结束谈话后，陶德曼博士向我表示，他认为这次谈话非常成功。

并非最后通牒
“陶德曼博士还在南京告诉蒋将军，这些条件并非最后通牒。德国大使在返程途中从船上经东京向柏林发送了一份电报，但后续发展尚不清楚，因为此后陶德曼博士尚未收到回复，”徐先生的报告 concludes。
“去年12月28日，在一封致最高国防会议的信中，我（汪精卫先生）陈述如下：‘去年12月初，在南京尚未陷落时，陶德曼博士在与蒋介石将军的会晤中提出的日本建议条件，不如我们现在面前的条件那样明确，反而更为苛刻，然而蒋介石将军考虑到局势的最终走向，同意将这些条件作为和平谈判的基础。
“如上所见，很清楚，我 thus 陈述的内容是非常具体的。
“如果要求提供更多证据，我将能够列举一百或一千更多的事实；但由于这些事情尚未成为过去，为了国家利益，有必要保密

page_data.en:
for the benefit of the country. As
for the mediation by the German
Ambassador, it has already become
a thing of the past, so I have cited
it as only one of the examples.

Three Questions

"My statement coming to this
point, there arise three questions.
They are as follows:
"1.—In comparing the proposals
of the German Ambassador with
the statement by Prince Konoye,
while the former were thus re-
garded as a basis for peace nego-
tiations, how can it be that the lat-
ter should be regarded as incapable
of being such a basis?
"2.—At the time the German
Ambassador was making efforts for
mediation, Nanking had not yet
fallen, but there was approval of
the starting of peace negotiations.
At the time when the statement by
Prince Konoye was issued, Nan-
king had already fallen and Tsinan,
Hsuchow, Kaifeng, Anking, Kiu-
kiang, Hangchow and the Wuhan
area also had collapsed, and though
Changsha had not yet fallen, it
had been reduced to ashes. When
there was a proposal for peace
negotiations, the answer was no.
What was the reason for such
rejection?
"3.—When the German Ambas-
sador was making efforts for peace
mediation, the members of the
Supreme National Defence Confer-
ence, whether they were at Nan-
king or in the Wuhan area, were
of one mind and expressed their
approval of negotiations for peace.
When the statement by Prince
Konoye was issued, however, there
were divisions among them with
regard to the conclusion of peace,
and those who were in the opposite
camp were subjected to abuse and
slander; more than that, even the
taking of life was resorted to, thus
making it impossible to work for
the benefit of the country. What
is the reason for all this?

Principles Of Peace Or War

"Though I do not ask for answers
to the above three questions, I can-
not but say something more to the
people in general regarding the
fundamental principles of peace or
war.
"Some people may say that as
they are maintaining their attitude
in favour of fighting, they have no
ear for arguments for peace, but
such reasoning is not warranted.
"The aim of the State is its
existence and independence, and
peace or war is nothing but the
means to that end And we fight
when we have to fight, and we
make peace when we have to do
so.
"Whether the making of peace
observes approval or not depends
upon the conditions of peace; if
such conditions are detrimental to
existence and independence, then
we should not make peace, but if
they are otherwise, then we should
make peace.
"Though there are some people
who say that China is able to at-
tain her unity only by means of
resistance, and that if she concludes
peace just now, she will again be
reduced to a state of disunity, I
cannot subscribe to such an opin-
ion.

三个问题

“我的陈述至此，出现了三个问题。它们如下：
“1.—在比较德国大使的提议与近卫亲王的声明时，既然前者被视为和平谈判的基础，为何后者却被视为不能作为此类基础？
“2.—在德国大使努力进行调停时，南京尚未陷落，但启动和平谈判获得了批准。在近卫亲王发表声明时，南京已经陷落，济南、徐州、开封、安庆、九江、杭州以及武汉地区也已沦陷，虽然长沙尚未陷落，但已化为灰烬。当有人提出和平谈判建议时，得到的回答是否定的。这种拒绝的原因是什么？
“3.—当德国大使努力进行和平调停时，最高国防会议的成员，无论是在南京还是在武汉地区，都同心协力，表示赞成和平谈判。然而，当近卫亲王的声明发表时，他们在缔结和平问题上出现了分歧，持反对立场的人遭受辱骂和诽谤；不仅如此，甚至诉诸夺人性命，使得为国家利益工作变得不可能。这一切的原因是什么？

和平或战争的原则

“虽然我不要求对上述三个问题作出回答，但我不能不对大众就和平或战争的基本原则多说几句。
“有些人可能会说，由于他们保持主战态度，因此听不进主和的论点，但这种推理是没有根据的。
“国家的目标是其生存和独立，和平或战争不过是达到这一目标的手段。我们在必须战斗时战斗，在必须和平时讲和。
“缔结和平是否获得认可，取决于和平的条件；如果这些条件有害于生存和独立，那么我们就不应讲和，但如果情况相反，那么我们就应该讲和。
“虽然有人说，中国只能通过抵抗来实现统一，如果现在缔结和平，中国将再次陷入分裂状态，但我不能赞同这种观点。

page_data.en:
Motive For Resistance
"If resistance is for the sake of
the existence and independence of
the State, then it is quite a differ-
ent question; but if resistance is
resorted to as a means of bringing
about internal unity, then I am
absolutely against it.
"While insistence upon conclu-
sion of peace does not prevent the
establishment of unity in the State,
opposition to conclusion of peace is
not necessarily the means of sav-
ing the State from disunity.
"There is another argument to
the effect that talk about conclu-
sion of peace affords an opportunity
to the Communist Party for start-
ing disturbances. But the policies
in favour of making disturbances
are inherent in the Communist
Party and they undergo no change
in case of either peace or war.
"If it can be said that at the
time of peace talks the machina-
tions of the Community Party come
to the surface, now should be the
time for suppressing its activities.
"There is yet another argument
that third Powers do not wish for
the conclusion of peace. But diplo-
macy should by all means be in-
dependent and China should decide
for herself whether she should
make peace or war, weighing well
which may be good for the exist-
ence of her state and race, and
there is no necessity to consider the
positions of other countries.
"The humiliating peace concluded
after the Sino-Japanese War has
brought to the country distress and
difficulty, and, therefore, we do not
wish for such temporary peace.
Though France concluded a humi-
liating peace after the Franco-
Prussian War and avenged herself
after the Great War to her great
satisfaction, we do not wish for such
temporary peace.
"Such a vicious circle of retalia-
tion will never bring about an in-
ternal peace.
"What I wish for from the bottom
of my heart is a far-sighted plan
for East Asia.
Need For Co-Existence
"I have no doubt that it is as
clear as day that if Japan and
China fight with each other, they
will both suffer damage, and if they
conclude peace they will both en-
joy co-existence.
"If the two countries co-operate
with each other for peace, they will
certainly be able to bring about
everlasting stability in East Asia,
and if not, they will both suffer
damage and both come to collapse.
"Though, on the one hand, the
peoples of the two countries are
sceptical about this point, yet on the
other hand they have some kind of
firm belief in this matter.
"After 20 months of fierce fighting,
Japan has suffered a great deal,
and China also has suffered no small
sacrifice; thus, they both have been
injured and are rushing along the
common road to destruction. At
the same time, it is clear beyond
doubt that the paths of both to co-
existence and co-prosperity are one
and the same.
"It is a great wonder to me why
the enlightened peoples of both
countries, for fear of temporary
vicissitudes and vulgar criticisms,
are faltering in their attitude and
thus have not decided upon what
course to take. I wish that they
would base their attitude upon a
spirit of independence and persever-
ance.
"The first sacrifice to proposals
for the conclusion of peace, Dr.
Tseng Chung-ming has marked with
his own blood the way for us to
travel onward to co-existence and
co-development.
"The last things that I want to
discuss are the following:
page_data.zh:
抵抗的动机
“如果抵抗是为了国家的生存和独立，那么这就是一个完全不同的问题；但如果将抵抗作为实现内部统一的手段，那我绝对反对。
“虽然坚持缔结和平并不妨碍国家统一的建立，但反对缔结和平也不一定是使国家免于分裂的手段。
“还有一种论点认为，谈论缔结和平为共产党发动骚乱提供了机会。但是，制造骚乱的政策是共产党固有的，无论是和平还是战争时期，这些政策都不会改变。
“如果说在和平谈判期间，共产党的阴谋活动浮出水面，那么现在正是镇压其活动的时候。
“还有另一种论点认为，第三国不希望缔结和平。但是，外交无论如何应当独立，中国应根据什么有利于其国家和民族的生存，自行决定是战是和，没有必要考虑其他国家的立场。
“中日战争后缔结的屈辱性和约给国家带来了苦难和困境，因此，我们不希望这种暂时的和平。虽然法国在普法战争后缔结了屈辱性和约，并在大战后得以雪耻，令其大为满意，但我们不希望这种暂时的和平。
“这种报复的恶性循环永远不会带来内部和平。
“我衷心希望的是有一个远大的东亚计划。
共存的需要
“我毫不怀疑，显而易见的是，如果日本和中国相互交战，双方都将遭受损害，而如果它们缔结和平，双方都将享受共存。
“如果两国为和平而合作，它们肯定能够实现东亚的永久稳定，否则，双方都将遭受损害并走向崩溃。
“虽然一方面两国人民对此持怀疑态度，但另一方面他们对此事也有某种坚定的信念。
“经过20个月的激烈战斗，日本遭受了巨大损失，中国也付出了不小的牺牲；因此，双方都受了伤，正沿着共同的毁灭之路狂奔。同时，毫无疑问，双方通往共存共荣的道路是同一条。
“令我大为不解的是，为什么两国的开明人士因为害怕暂时的变故和庸俗的批评，而在态度上犹豫不决，从而未能决定采取何种方针。我希望他们能以独立和坚韧的精神为基础来确立自己的态度。
“曾仲明博士为和平提议做出了第一个牺牲，他用鲜血为我们标出了通往共存与共发展的道路。
“我最后要讨论的是以下几点：

page_data.en:
Urged To Go Abroad
"In the middle of February, the Chungking Government dispatched a member of the Central Executive Council to me and tried to persuade me to go abroad by the grant of a passport
"At the time I entrusted to him my answer to the Chungking Government, which was as follows:
"1.—It would have been impossible for me to issue a statement if I had not left Chungking, but at this time of difficulties for our country, it was a heart-breaking action for me to leave Chungking. And now, how can I leave the country? I wanted to leave Chungking because I wanted to express the reasons why my contentions should be accepted, not because I bore any grievances against individual persons.
"2.—I am told that the Nationalist Government is making efforts for the promotion of international mediation. If, at least, they intend to carry on direct negotiations side by side with international mediation, then I will not be unwilling to offer my lateral co-operation and efforts, although I am not holding any public position.
"3.—If the Nationalist Government only postpones making any decision and thus lets the current situation drift by missing a favourable opportunity, I shall only have to come back home again even if I once go out of the country.
"It is certain that the above contentions of mine constituted the principal cause of the incident of March 21.
"It is very regrettable that Dr. Tseng Chung-ming, who had a long life before him, has died without witnessing the fulfilment of his desires. If possible, I would have taken his place to be assassinated.
Peril Of Association
"Though there is no knowing when I shall fall a victim at the hands of an assassin following the publication of this statement, it would be only what I wish for. I wish that the people of my country will read these words, which I leave behind me, and will appreciate what I have contended in them.
"What I have contended is the indispensable way for China to maintain her existence and independence, and, at the same time, the indispensable way to bring about eternal peace in East Asia and the world.
"My contentions cannot be accepted by the Chungking Government for the present, but I shall be gratified if, some day in the future, they will be accepted by the people of the country or by the peoples of both Japan and China."—Domei.
page_data.zh:
被劝出国
“二月中旬，重庆政府派遣一名中央执行委员来见我，试图通过授予护照来说服我出国。
“当时我委托他向重庆政府转达我的答复，内容如下：
“1.——如果我没有离开重庆，我就不可能发表声明，但在国家困难之际，离开重庆对我来说是一件令人心碎的事。而现在，我怎么能离开这个国家呢？我想离开重庆是因为我想表达我的主张应被接受的理由，而不是因为我对任何个人怀有怨恨。
“2.——据说国民政府正在努力促进国际调停。如果他们至少打算在进行国际调停的同时进行直接谈判，那么即使我不担任任何公职，我也不愿意提供侧面的合作和努力。
“3.——如果国民政府只是推迟做出任何决定，从而错失良机，让当前局势听之任之，那么即使我一旦出国，我也只能再次回国。
“可以肯定的是，我的上述主张构成了三月二十一日事件的主要原因。
“非常遗憾的是，曾仲明博士来日方长，却在愿望实现之前去世。如果可能的话，我愿代他遇刺身亡。
交往的危险
“虽然不知道在这份声明发表后，我何时会成为刺客手中的受害者，但这正是我所希望的。我希望我国人民能阅读我留下的这些话，并理解我在其中所主张的内容。
“我所主张的是中国维持其生存和独立的必由之路，同时也是实现东亚和世界永久和平的必由之路。
“我的主张目前不能被重庆政府接受，但如果将来有一天能被全国人民或中日两国人民所接受，我将感到欣慰。”——同盟社。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

FEB 6 1939

Mrs. Wang Ching-wei's
Brother Arrested

Charged With Misuse of
Public Funds

Word has been received in Shanghai
to the effect that a brother-in-law of
Mr. Wang Ching-wei, dismissed Kuo-
mintang statesman who favours peace
with Japan, has been arrested in
Mengtze.
He is Chen Chang-tsu, director of
the Aero Manufacturing Factory in
Kunming and brother of Madame
Wang Ching-wei, popularly known as
Chen Bih-chuan, one of a few women
members of the Central Executive
Committee of the Kuomintang.
He is alleged to have fled from his
post carrying a large sum of money.
His disappearance was reported on
January 16 but quickly the Military
Affairs Council ordered all branch
offices to look for him and he was
eventually arrested a few days ago in
a flying school in Mengtze.
He will be court-martialled.

《字林西报》，

1939年2月6日

汪精卫之弟被捕

被控滥用公款

上海收到消息，称主张与日本和平的前国民党政治家汪精卫先生的一位妹夫在蒙自被捕。
此人名叫陈昌祖，是昆明航空制造厂厂长，也是汪精卫夫人（俗称陈璧君，国民党中央执行委员会中为数不多的女性成员之一）的弟弟。
据称他携巨款潜逃离职。他的失踪于1月16日被报告，但军事委员会迅速命令各分支机构搜寻他，几天前他最终在蒙自的一所飞行学校被捕。
他将受到军法审判。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

JAN 26 1939

RUMOUR CONCERNING
WANG CHING-WEI

Visit Of Hsu Shih-ying
To Chinese Leader
Given Denial .

HONGKONG, Jan. 25. Japanese
reports reaching here from Hanoi
definitely deny rumours that the
former Chinese Ambassador to
Japan, Hsu Shih-ying has arrived
in that city to visit Wang Ching-
wei.
The reports had asserted that
Hsu Shih-ying had travelled to
Hanoi on instructions from General
Chiang Kai-shek in order to
endeavour to persuade Wang Ching-
wei to return to Chungking.
According to the Japanese re-
ports, the police protection of Wang
Ching-wei at an undisclosed place
in Indo-China has been intensified
after the arrival of reports from
Hongkong of an attempted as-
sassination of Lam Pak-sang.—
Transocean.

1939年1月26日

关于汪精卫的谣言

徐世英拜访中国领导人
一事遭否认

香港，1月25日。从河内传到这里的日本报道明确否认了前中国驻日本大使徐世英已抵达该市拜访汪精卫的谣言。
此前的报道声称，徐世英是奉蒋介石将军的指示前往河内，试图说服汪精卫返回重庆。
根据日本方面的报道，在香港传来林柏生遇刺未遂的消息后，位于印度支那某隐蔽地点的汪精卫的警方保护力度已经加强。——跨洋通讯社。

WANG'S FOLLOWER HERE
Mei Shih-ping, one of the follow-
ers of Wang Ching-wei, ousted Kuo-
mintang leader, is reported to have
secretly arrived in Shanghai Mei,
emerged into the limelight when he

follower of Wang, handed the "peace
message" of their leader to the
Chinese press in Hongkong last
month.

page_data.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JAN 1 7 1939

Wang's Departure
Not Secret
Chungking Knew He Was
Going, Says Tseng Chung-
Ming; Opinions Differed

Hanoi, Jan. 16.
Allegations that Mr. Wang Ching-
wei, dismissed Deputy Executive of
the Kuomintang, left Chungking
without notifying the Nationalist
authorities, were refuted here today
by Mr. Tseng Chung-ming, former
Vice-Minister of Communications,
who is accompanying Mr. Wang.
The late Nationalist official said
he doubted the report that Gen.
Chiang Kai-shek was sending Mr.
T. V. Soong, chairman of the Board
of Directors of the Bank of China,
to Hanoi to urge Mr. Wang to go
abroad.
"Gen. Chiang's group is trying to
disseminate the rumour that Mr.
Wang came to Hanoi suddenly,"
declared Mr. Tseng in an interview
with Domei, "but the fact is that
Mr. Wang had two serious discussions
on the question of peace with Gen.
Chiang prior to his departure from
Chungking. Realizing that their
divergence of opinions was such that
it could not be surmounted, Mr.
Wang openly left the Kuomintang
capital," Mr. Tseng said, speaking on
behalf of Mr. Wang.
Mr. Wang's health has been show-
ing signs of improvement recently.
He changed his residence for the
third time since his arrival in Hanoi
a month ago, on Saturday night.—
Domei.

Another Denunciation

Chungking, Jan. 16.
General Liao-Luai, Governor of
Anhwei province, General Chang
Chi-chung, Governor of Hunan pro-
vince, and General Liu Wen-hui,
Governor of Sikong province, have
joined other leaders in telegraphing
to the Government voicing their
support of the Government's decision
to expel Mr. Wang Ching-wei.

Talks with Japanese at Hanoi
Mr. Wang Ching-wei is at present
engaged in negotiations with certain
Japanese in Hanoi, according to
arrivals here from that city.—Reuter.
