《字林西报》，

1939年1月17日

汪的离去
并非秘密
曾仲明称重庆知情；
意见存在分歧

河内，1月16日。
有关被罢免的国民党副总裁汪精卫先生在未通知国民政府当局的情况下离开重庆的说法，今天在此间陪同汪先生的前交通部副部长曾仲明先生予以驳斥。
这位已故的国民政府官员表示，他怀疑有关蒋介石将军派遣中国银行董事会主席宋子文先生前往河内敦促汪先生出国的报道。
“蒋氏集团正试图散布汪先生突然来到河内的谣言，”曾先生在接受同盟社采访时宣称，“但事实是，汪先生在离开重庆之前，就和平问题与蒋将军进行了两次严肃的讨论。意识到他们的意见分歧无法克服，汪先生公开离开了国民党首都，”曾先生代表汪先生说道。
汪先生的健康状况最近显示出好转的迹象。自一个月前抵达河内以来，他在周六晚上第三次更换了住所。——同盟社。

另一项谴责

重庆，1月16日。
安徽省主席廖磊将军、湖南省主席张治中将军和西康省主席刘文辉将军与其他领导人一起致电政府，表示支持政府驱逐汪精卫先生的决定。

在河内与日本人会谈
根据从该市传来的消息，汪精卫目前正在河内与某些日本人进行谈判。——路透社。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES
JAN 1 1 1939

Tokyo Newspapers Urge
“Wait And See” Policy
On Wang’s Peace Move

Significant Passages Pointed Out And Tribute
Paid To His Moral Courage; Chiang Regime
Is Seen Threatened With Split

BUT QUICK WITHDRAWAL OF JAPANESE
TROOPS SAID IMPOSSIBILITY

TOKYO, Jan. 100.—A “wait and see” policy is advocated by newspapers here to-day in commenting on the open letter addressed by Mr. Wang Ching-wei to the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang Party and the Supreme War Council.

Newspapers pay special attention to the passages in Mr. Wang Ching-wei’s letter, in which he says:

“This opportunity to end the present war must not be allowed to pass again”; and “Assistance from Great Britain, the United States and France is gradually materializing, but such assistance can only have the effect of putting us into a more favourable position to negotiate peace; it is by no means sufficient to have any effect on the outcome of the war, enabling us to secure a decisive victory by military measures.”

The “Miyako Shimbun” pays tribute to Mr. Wang Ching-wei for “his moral courage in advocating peace, which is so badly wanted by the Chinese people, but which leaders of the Kuomintang Government still hesitate to voice.”

The “Nichi Nichi” is of the opinion that the most important and significant part of Mr. Wang Ching-wei’s letter consists in the limit foreseen by him to the assistance from Great Britain, the United States and France.

Because, the paper asserts, “there are inseparable connections between General Chiang Kai-shek’s resistance against Japan and the assistance from these three countries, of which General Chiang Kai-shek so boastfully exaggerated to his people.”

No Decisive Factor

The assistance of these three countries, the paper continues, provides no decisive factor in the China Incident,” nor can it affect Japan’s firm determination to build up a “new order in East Asia.”

The crux of the question, declares the paper, resolves into an interpretation of Prince Konoye’s statement on December 22 by those “far-sighted Chinese people who share Japanese ideals and aspirations.”

Communist Influence

The paper asserts that the passage in Mr. Wang Ching-wei’s open letter in which he says: “With the exception of the Communist Party and minorities who would like to see China ruined, the National Government overthrown and the Kuomintang collapse, I can see no reason why anyone should be opposed to an honourable peace” should be read with grave concern not only by China, but also by third Powers.

A couple of months will be required to see what the real effects of the message and letter of Mr. Wang Ching-wei will exert on China, according to the “Kokumin Shimbun,” which points out that it is impossible to expect the Chiang Kai-shek regime to make a volte face with Mr. Wang Ching-wei’s peace move.

Threatened Split

“There is no gainsaying, however,” the paper adds, “that Chinese public opinion is now divided and the Chiang Kai-shek Government is threatened with a split as a result of Mr. Wang Ching-wei’s bold message and open letter.”

As regards the terms of peace suggested by Mr. Wang Ching-wei, the “Kokumin Shimbun” declares: “They cannot be accepted by Japan as a basis for negotiation. A meeting point will be found regarding the respect for the sovereignty and territory of China, the questions of the conclusion of the anti-Comintern pact and economic co-operation.”

Peace And Order Wanted

However, the paper points out the absolute impossibility of a complete and quick withdrawal of Japanese troops from China.

“Not a single Japanese soldier now in China,” the paper concludes, “wants to leave the continent until and unless real peace and order are established.—Reuter.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年1月11日

东京报纸呼吁
对汪精卫的和平举动采取“观望”政策

指出重要段落并赞扬其道德勇气；蒋政权被视为面临分裂威胁

但称日军迅速撤军是不可能的

东京，1月10日电。——这里的报纸今天在评论汪精卫先生致国民党中央执行委员会和最高国防会议的公开信时，主张采取“观望”政策。

各报特别关注汪精卫先生信中的以下段落，他说：

“结束当前战争的这一机会绝不可再次错过”；以及“来自英国、美国和法国的援助正在逐渐实现，但这种援助只能使我们在谈判和平时处于更有利的地位；它绝不足以对战争结果产生任何影响，使我们能够通过军事手段获得决定性胜利。”

《都新闻》赞扬汪精卫先生“倡导和平的道德勇气，这是中国人民迫切需要的，但国民党政府的领导人仍犹豫不敢发声。”

《日日新闻》认为，汪精卫先生信件中最重要和最具意义的部分在于他对英、美、法三国援助限度的预见。

因为该报声称，“蒋介石将军的抗日行动与这三个国家的援助之间有着不可分割的联系，而蒋介石将军曾向他的人民夸大地吹嘘过这种援助。”

非决定性因素

该报继续称，这三个国家的援助“在‘中国事变’中不提供任何决定性因素”，也不能影响日本建立“东亚新秩序”的坚定决心。

该报宣称，问题的关键在于那些“拥有与日本相同理想和愿望的有远见的中国人”对近卫亲王12月22日声明的解释。

共产主义的影响

该报声称，汪精卫先生公开信中说：“除了共产党和少数希望看到中国毁灭、国民政府被推翻、国民党崩溃的人之外，我看不到任何人反对体面和平的理由”，这一段不仅应引起中国的严重关切，也应引起第三国的严重关切。

据《国民新闻》报道，需要几个月的时间才能看清汪精卫先生的信息和信件对中国产生的实际效果，该报指出，不能指望蒋介石政权因汪精卫的和平举动而突然改变立场。

面临分裂威胁

然而，该报补充说：“不可否认的是，由于汪精卫大胆的信息和公开信，中国舆论现在出现分歧，蒋介石政府面临分裂的威胁。”

关于汪精卫先生建议的和平条款，《国民新闻》宣称：“日本不能接受这些条款作为谈判的基础。在尊重中国主权和领土、签订反共协定以及经济合作等问题上，将会找到共同点。”

渴望和平与秩序

然而，该报指出，日军完全且迅速从中国撤军是绝对不可能的。

该报总结道：“目前在中国的任何一名日本士兵，除非真正的和平与秩序得以建立，否则都不愿离开大陆。”——路透社。

S. G. REGIS
S. B. D.

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
JAN 10 1939

NOTHING NEW

One important fact emerges from the latest declaration made by Mr. Wang Ching-wei amplifying the telegram sent to Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, advocating that China should come to terms with Japan. Mr. Wang states that on December 9 he expounded his point of view to the General Executive of the Kuomintang, the Generalissimo, that the difficulties confronting China arose out of the problem of how to sustain the war, and that with regard to Japan they arose out of the problem of how to end it, that both realized their own particular difficulties as well as the difficulties of the other, and that, therefore, peace was not an impossibility. That view was not accepted by Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, and in due course Mr. Wang Ching-wei withdrew from the interior. He then sent the famous telegram which was also liberated to the Press, since when he has been expelled from the Kuomintang. When a responsible statesman gives his views to the head of his Government, and finds them to be unacceptable, if he is an honest man he resigns. Had Mr. Wang done only that there could have been no grounds for criticism, but that he aided his country's enemy by broadcasting his views in the manner he did is undeniable, and he is fortunate that no severer charge has been laid against him than that of lack of discipline. Apart from that fact it is interesting to note Mr. Wang's contention in the course of this latest declaration. He says:—

"The statement issued by the Japanese Government on December 22 indicated that Japan has come to the proper realization of her position with regard to China. It may be recalled that although the terms proposed by Japan through the intermediary of the German Ambassador, prior to the fall of Nanking in the early part of December last year (1937), were more unfavourable and even less definite, yet Gen. Chiang, in view of the general situation, had no hesitation in accepting them as the basis on which to negotiate an honourable peace.

The revelation concerning Chiang Kai-shek's attitude to those peace overtures is probably the divulging of a piece of secret history, but the fact is that the terms put forward by Dr. Trautmann were emphatically rejected, and that is all that matters.

The question naturally arises as to whether in reality the terms offered to China through German intermediation were really worse than those which were contained in Prince Konoye's recent declaration. In December, 1937, it was stated that the terms received by Dr. Herbert von Dircksen, German Ambassador to Tokyo, for transmission to the Chinese Government were :—

1. Conclusion of a Sino-Japanese economic agreement granting Japan participation in China's national resources, Customs, communications and transport.
2. China's adherence to the anti-Comintern pact.
3. Stationing of permanent Japanese garrisons in China.
4. Creation of demilitarized zones in areas specified by Japan.
5. Formation of an independent government in Inner Mongolia.
6. Payment of war reparations by China.

There were it will be noticed six conditions. Prince Konoye in his latest declaration reduced them to five:—

1. Establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Manchukuo.
2. The conclusion of an anti-Comintern agreement between China and Japan.
3. The stationing of Japanese troops in China and the designation of Inner Mongolia as a special anti-Communist area.
4. Recognition of the freedom of residence and trade for Japanese in the interior of China.
5. Extension to Japan of facilities for the development of China's natural resources, especially in North China and Inner Mongolia.

It will be noticed that the main difference between the two sets of terms is the omission now of the demand for the payment of war reparations by China. With that major exception the two sets of terms are practically identical, except for the manner in which they have been phrased, though to the latter should be added the possibility of Japanese relinquishing extraterritoriality and securing the retrocession of the Concessions to China.

Comparison of the terms does not permit of the conclusion that those presented after the fall of Nanking are very much more onerous than those which are offered now. Glib phrases concerning the preservation of China's sovereignty and territorial integrity are meaningless in the light of Prince Konoye's utterances, for with the stationing of Japanese troops in China, the Chinese will have just about the same degree of sovereignty and integrity as they did under the Manchus with their garrisons of bannermen to hold them in subjection. Instead of the formation of an independent Government in Inner Mongolia, the designation of that territory as an anti-Communist area is suggested. The difference is surely but in name alone, and indeed except for a difference in order and phraseology the two sets of terms, so far as five in each are concerned, might be considered as identical, for what is not clearly expressed in one can be definitely inferred from the other. Why has the claim for an indemnity been dropped? Obviously because by the economic arrangements Japan is busily engaged in perfecting it is hoped to wrest profits which may be substituted for the indemnity originally required. Monopolistic control of China's economic system, and its exploitation along lines which have already been indicated by the action of the Japanese themselves demonstrate that they are confident of making their military venture pay in the future. Thus with a complete stranglehold upon China's industry and commerce Japan should be able to reimburse herself, and the claim for an indemnity can consequently be dropped. The recognition of Manchoukuo specifically demanded by Prince Konoye is obviously contained in the earlier demand that China should adhere to the anti-Comintern Pact: she could not very well do so without acknowledging the sovereignty of the provinces she has lost in the north. The earlier requirement of the creation of demilitarized zones can only mean such zones as those which are not occupied by Japanese troops, and when the two sets of conditions are thus compared Mr. Wang Ching-wei's contention that those offered after the fall of Nanking were far more onerous will be seen to have very little merit about it. The substance of Japan's original demands has been repeated, and consequently emphasized.

《字林西报》，
1939年1月10日

并无新意

汪精卫先生最近发表声明，进一步阐述发给蒋介石委员长的电报，主张中国与日本讲和，从中显现出一个重要事实。汪先生表示，他在12月9日向国民党总裁、委员长阐述了他的观点，即中国面临的困难源于如何维持战争的问题，而关于日本，困难源于如何结束战争，双方都认识到各自的特殊困难以及对方的困难，因此，和平并非不可能。这一观点未被蒋介石委员长接受，随后汪精卫离开了内地。他随后发出了著名的通电，该通电也向新闻界发布，此后他被开除出国民党。当一位负责任的政治家向政府首脑提出观点，却发现不被接受时，如果他是诚实的人，他就会辞职。如果汪先生仅止于此，便没有批评的依据，但他以这种方式广播其观点从而协助了国家的敌人，这是不可否认的，幸运的是，对他提出的指控没有比缺乏纪律更严厉的。除了这一事实外，值得注意的是汪先生在这份最新声明中的论点。他说：—

“日本政府12月22日发表的声明表明，日本已正确认识到其对华立场。回想一下，尽管去年（1937年）12月初南京陷落之前，日本通过德国大使中介提出的条件更为不利甚至更不明确，但蒋将军鉴于总体局势，毫不犹豫地接受它们作为谈判体面和平的基础。

关于蒋介石对这些和平试探态度的披露可能是泄露了一段秘史，但事实是，陶德曼博士提出的条件被坚决拒绝，这才是关键所在。

自然会产生这样一个问题：实际上，通过德国中介向中国提供的条件是否真的比近卫亲王最近声明中包含的条件更糟糕。1937年12月，据说驻东京德国大使狄克逊博士收到的拟转交中国政府的条件如下：—

1. 签订中日经济协定，允许日本参与中国的国家资源、海关、通讯和运输。
2. 中国加入反共产国际协定。
3. 在中国驻扎永久性的日本守备队。
4. 在日本指定的地区建立非军事区。
5. 在内蒙古成立独立政府。
6. 中国支付战争赔款。

请注意，共有六个条件。近卫亲王在其最新声明中将它们减少为五个：—

1. 中国与满洲国建立外交关系。
2. 中日签订反共产国际协定。
3. 日军驻扎中国，并将内蒙古指定为特殊的反共区域。
4. 承认日本人在中国内地的居住和贸易自由。
5. 向日本提供开发中国自然资源的便利，特别是在华北和内蒙古。

请注意，两套条件的主要区别在于现在省略了中国支付战争赔款的要求。除了这一主要例外外，两套条件几乎相同，只是措辞方式不同，尽管对于后者还应加上日本放弃治外法权并将租界归还中国的可能性。

比较这些条件并不能得出南京陷落后提出的条件比现在提供的条件繁重得多的结论。在近卫亲王的言论背景下，关于维护中国主权和领土完整的华丽辞藻毫无意义，因为随着日军驻扎中国，中国人拥有的主权和完整程度将与他们在满清统治下、由八旗驻防军控制以使其臣服时的程度大致相同。与其在内蒙古成立独立政府，不如将该地区指定为反共区域。这种区别肯定只是名义上的，事实上，除了顺序和措辞的不同外，就每套五个条件而言，这两套条件可以被视为相同，因为一套中未明确表达的内容可以从另一套中明确推断出来。为什么放弃了赔款要求？显然，是因为希望通过日本正忙于完善的经济安排来攫取利润，以替代最初要求的赔款。对中国经济体系的垄断控制，以及按照日本人自身行动所指示路线进行的剥削，表明他们有信心使其军事冒险在未来获利。因此，通过完全扼住中国工商业的咽喉，日本应该能够自我补偿，因此可以放弃赔款要求。近卫亲王特别要求的承认满洲国，显然包含在早期要求中国加入反共产国际协定的要求中：如果不承认其在北方失去省份的主权，她很难做到这一点。早期要求建立非军事区只能意味着那些未被日军占领的区域，当这样比较两套条件时，汪精卫先生声称南京陷落后提供的条件繁重得多的论点就显得没有什么价值了。日本原始要求的实质已被重复，并因此得到强调。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

JAN 8 1939

Another Denial of
Peace Moves

“Clumsy Attempt to
Mislead Public”

London, Jan. 6.
Mr. Quo Tai-chi, Chinese Ambassador to London, today emphatically denied he had supported the recent proposal for peace talks with Japan advanced by Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
Mr. Quo, along with the Chinese Ambassadors to Washington and Paris were alleged to have cabled Gen. Chiang Kai-shek urging him to follow Mr. Wang's suggestion. The allegation was made in pamphlets dropped on the International Settlement in Shanghai on Thursday by Japanese planes.
The Chinese Ambassador here said that instead of supporting Mr. Wang, he actively attempted to dissuade the former Kuomintang official from issuing his circular telegram to Government officials urging peace talks on the condition that all Japanese troops would be withdrawn from China.
“The Chinese Ambassador categorically denied as absolutely false the Japanese report alleging he telegraphed Chungking urging the acceptance of Wang Ching-wei's peace proposals,” a statement issued by the Chinese Embassy here said. “Far from being any foundation for such allegations, Mr. Quo, as a close friend of Mr. Wang, sent him telegrams strongly urging him to abandon his **〔此处转录不清〕** The Japanese report is a deliberate, but clumsy, attempt to mislead the public and create confusion.”
--United Press.

1939年1月8日

再次否认
和平举动

“误导公众的拙劣尝试”

伦敦，1月6日电。
中国驻伦敦大使郭泰祺先生今天 emphatically 否认他支持汪精卫先生最近提出的与日本进行和平谈判的建议。
据称，郭先生与驻华盛顿和巴黎的中国大使一起致电蒋介石将军，敦促他遵循汪先生的建议。这一指控出现在周四由日本飞机在上海公共租界散发的传单中。
此处的中国大使表示，他非但没有支持汪先生，反而积极试图劝阻这位前国民党官员不要向政府官员发出循环通电，以所有日军撤出中国为条件呼吁和平谈判。
“中国大使馆在此发表声明称：‘中国大使断然否认日本报道中称他致电重庆敦促接受汪精卫和平提议的说法，称其完全虚假。’‘此类指控毫无根据，郭先生作为汪先生的挚友，曾向他发送电报，强烈敦促他放弃其**〔此处转录不清〕**。日本的报道是一种故意但拙劣的误导公众和制造混乱的尝试。’”
——合众社。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
China Should Respond To
Statement By Tokyo, Says
Mr. Wang To Party C.E.C.
（印：POLICE REGISTRY JAN 9 1939）

Japan's Reconsideration Of Her Attitude Towards
China Is An Opportunity To End War Which
"Must Not Be Allowed To Pass Again"

FULL TEXT OF HISTORIC TELEGRAM
DISPATCHED ON DECEMBER. 28

HONGKONG, Jan. 3.—Japan's "reconsideration" of her attitude towards China, exemplified in the December 22 statement of Prince Ayamaro Konoye, former Japanese Premier, constitutes an "opportunity to end the present war" which "must not be allowed to pass again."

This statement was made by Mr. Wang Ching-wei, former Deputy Chief Executive of the Kuomintang, in a telegram dispatched to the Central Executive Committee of the party and the Chinese Supreme National Defence Council on December 28. The full text of the telegram, amplifying that sent by Mr. Wang to General Chiang Kai-shek which was published on December 31, was made public here to-night.

"With the exception of the Communist Party and a minority, who would like to see China doomed, the Nationalist Government overthrown, and the Kuomintang collapse," Mr. Wang declared, he could "see no proper reason why anybody should be opposed to honourable peace."

"It may be recalled," Mr. Wang's message said, "that although the terms proposed by Japan through the German Ambassador, prior to the fall of Nanking in the early part of December last year (1937), were more unfavourable and even less definite, yet General Chiang, in view of the general situation, had no hesitation in accepting them as a basis on which to negotiate an honourable peace."

Assistance from Great Britain and France, he continued, "can only have the effect of putting us in a more favourable position to negotiate peace; it is by no means sufficient to have any effect on the outcome of the war, enabling us to secure a decisive victory by military measures."

Germany and Italy, Mr. Wang asserted, "will certainly not be reluctant to assist in the re-establishment of peace."

Mr. Wang's Statement
Mr. Wang's statement was as follows:—
"On the 9th of this month (December 9, 1938), I expounded to the General Executive of the Kuomintang, General Chiang-Kai-shek, the view that the difficulties now confronting China arose out of the problem of how to sustain the war, that with regard to Japan they arose out of the problem of how to end the war, that both countries realized their own particular difficulties as well as the difficulties of the other, and that, therefore, peace is not an impossibility.

"In addition, I said that, on this issue, in so far as foreign relations were concerned, we might have expected the assistance of Great Britain, the United States and of France, the acquiescence of the Soviet Union, the non-intervention of Germany and Italy and especially the awakening of Japan. And if Japan should come to the realization of the fact that China could not be subjugated by force of arms nor could the Far East be brought under its absolute hegemony, then peace would eventually come to the relief of all. These views were known to all those comrades who were present at our conversation."

Japan's Realization
"The statement issued by the Japanese Government on December 22 indicated that Japan has come to the proper realization of her position with regard to China. It may be recalled that although the terms proposed by Japan through the intermediary of the German Ambassador, prior to the fall of Nanking in the early part of December last year (1937), were more unfavourable and even less definite, yet General Chiang, in view of the general situation, had no hesitation in accepting them as the basis on which to negotiate an honourable peace.

"Subsequently, however, as the result of Japan's own hesitation and change of mind, and the consequent alteration of the proposed terms and the widening of their scope after the fall of Nanking, the matter was left in abeyance. But in view of the present reconsideration of her attitude towards China by Japan, it is natural that we should respond with a statement on what basis we may negotiate with Japan in order to find a proper solution of the various questions with a view to re-establishing peace and stabilizing the Far Eastern situation. This opportunity to end the present war must not be allowed to pass again.

Aid From Third Powers
"Assistance from Great Britain, the United States and France is gradually materializing. But such assistance can only have the effect of putting us in a more favourable position to negotiate peace; it is by no means sufficient to have any effect on the outcome of the war, enabling us to secure a decisive victory by military measures. This is well known to everybody and needs no further explanation. With regard to international situation, it is obvious that without the co-operation of Great Britain, the United States and France, Soviet Russia cannot take any independent action to help China on any large scale, while Germany and Italy will certainly not be reluctant to assist in the re-establishment of peace. With regard to the internal situation—with the exception of the Communist Party and a minority, who would like to see China doomed, the National Government overthrown, and the Kuomintang collapse—I can see no proper reason why anybody should be opposed to honourable peace.

"It is only after mature deliberation that I venture to make this proposal. I have already expounded my views to General Chiang in another message, and I am now addressing this to you in the hope that my sincerity be given due consideration and my suggestions honoured with your approval."—Domei.

（手写批注：6 1/4）

《字林西报》。
汪先生对党中央执行委员会称，中国应回应东京的声明
（印：警务处登记 1939年1月9日）

日本重新考虑其对华态度是结束战争的契机，
“绝不可再次错失”

12月28日发出的历史性电报全文

香港，1月3日电——日本前首相近卫文麿亲王在12月22日的声明中体现出的日本对华态度的“重新考虑”，构成了一个“结束当前战争”的“绝不可再次错失”的契机。

此言出自国民党前副总裁汪精卫先生，他在12月28日发给该党中央执行委员会及中国最高国防委员会的电报中作了上述表示。今晚在此公布了该电报的全文，该电报对汪先生于12月31日公布的致蒋介石将军的电报内容进行了详述。

汪先生宣称，“除了共产党和少数希望看到中国灭亡、国民政府被推翻、国民党崩溃的人之外”，他“看不出任何人反对体面和平的正当理由”。

汪先生的电文称：“不妨回顾一下，尽管去年（1937年）12月上旬南京陷落之前，日本通过德国大使提出的条件更为不利甚至更不明确，但蒋介石将军鉴于总体局势，毫不犹豫地接受这些条件作为谈判体面和平的基础。”

他接着说，来自英国和法国的援助，“只能使我们在谈判和平时处于更有利的地位；这绝不足以对战争结果产生任何影响，使我们能够通过军事手段获得决定性胜利。”

汪先生断言，德国和意大利“肯定不会不愿协助重建和平”。

汪先生的声明
汪先生的声明如下：—
“本月9日（1938年12月9日），我向国民党总裁蒋介石将军阐述了我的观点，即中国目前面临的困难源于如何维持战争的问题，而就日本而言，困难源于如何结束战争的问题，两国都认识到各自的特殊困难以及对方的困难，因此，和平并非不可能。

“此外，我说，在这一问题上，就外交关系而言，我们本可期待英国、美国和法国的援助，苏联的默许，德国和意大利的不干涉，特别是日本的觉醒。如果日本意识到中国无法被武力征服，远东也无法置于其绝对霸权之下这一事实，那么和平最终将使各方得到解脱。这些观点为参加我们要谈的所有同志所知晓。”

日本的觉悟
“日本政府于12月22日发表的声明表明，日本已对其在华地位有了正确的认识。不妨回顾一下，尽管去年（1937年）12月上旬南京陷落之前，日本通过德国大使中介提出的条件更为不利甚至更不明确，但蒋介石将军鉴于总体局势，毫不犹豫地接受这些条件作为谈判体面和平的基础。

“然而，随后由于日本自身的犹豫和改变主意，以及在南京陷落后提议条件的相应变更和范围的扩大，此事被搁置。但鉴于日本目前重新考虑其对华态度，我们自然应当回应一份声明，说明我们可以基于何种基础与日本谈判，以便寻求各种问题的适当解决方案，旨在重建和平并稳定远东局势。这个结束当前战争的机会绝不可再次错失。

第三国的援助
“来自英国、美国和法国的援助正逐渐成为现实。但这种援助只能使我们在谈判和平时处于更有利的地位；它绝不足以对战争结果产生任何影响，使我们能够通过军事手段获得决定性胜利。这是众所周知的，无需进一步解释。就国际局势而言，显而易见，如果没有英国、美国和法国的合作，苏俄无法采取任何独立行动大规模援助中国，而德国和意大利肯定不会不愿协助重建和平。就国内局势而言——除了共产党和少数希望看到中国灭亡、国民政府被推翻、国民党崩溃的人之外——我看不出任何人反对体面和平的正当理由。

“经过深思熟虑后，我才敢提出这一建议。我已在另一封电报中向蒋介石将军阐述了我的观点，现在致函各位，希望我的诚意能得到应有的考虑，我的建议能获得你们的批准。”——同盟社。

（手写批注：6 1/4）

January 4, 1939.

JOURNAL DE SHANGHAI :

THE CASHIERING OF WANG CHING-WEI

The National Government has replied to Wang Ching-wei's manifesto in favour of peace by means of sanctions. The President of the Central Political Council has been shorn of his posts; he has also been expelled from the Kuomintang.

The fact that it was announced on the morrow of the day that Wang Ching-wei had secretly left Chungking, that his words and acts do not bind the National Government shows that Wang Ching-wei has not been in accord with his colleagues. The Permanent Committee of the Central Executive Committee on January 1 or 2 emphasized the gravity of Wang Ching-wei's action which was taken on his own initiative. The Committee reproached him with desertion of his post without permission, publishing peace proposals against the interests of the country and contrary to the decisions of the Government, showing in a false light the demands of the enemy in such a manner as to mislead the Chinese people, with having relations with the enemy and with having by his culpable intrigue risked the disorganization of the State. In conclusion, the Committee holds the view that Wang Ching-wei is proposing the capitulation of China.

In any other country the acts for which Wang Ching-wei is being criticized would be regarded as acts of treason. However, it seems that the Chungking Government does not regard the affair as being very grave since it is content with only adopting comparatively mild measures of repression. This is not the first time that Wang Ching-wei has been placed under a ban by the Government and the Kuomintang; his former condemnations did not stop him, after a lapse of time, from again taking his place in the counsels of the Government and of the Party and of even being called to the direction of the Government.

However, the weak points of his manifesto have been clearly exposed by his colleagues on the Central Executive Committee. It is inadmissible for a politician, in time of war, to decide, on his own initiative, to make peace or to permit him, by his intrigues, to divide or to weaken the Government entrusted with the defence of the nation. It would be equally strange for him to enter into relations with the enemy unless at the request of the Government. On the other hand, the Chungking Government is right when it says that Wang Ching-wei is misleading the people by presenting as sincere the assurances uttered by Prince Konoye and Mr. Arita in regard to the upholding of China's sovereignty, whereas the "new order of things" that Japan pretends to establish in the Far East will relegate China to a state of slavery like Manchukuo to-day. To accept the basis of peace which the Japanese have proposed would, as Wang Ching-wei's colleagues say, be tantamount to capitulation.

Now, Chungking considers it has sufficient means to continue the war. There is no lack of soldiers who are inured to the war and they will be fighting under more favourable conditions. Their armament is adequate

1939年1月4日。

《上海日报》：

汪精卫被撤职

国民政府已通过制裁措施回应了汪精卫支持和平的宣言。中央政治会议主席已被剥夺职务；他也被开除出国民党。

在汪精卫秘密离开重庆的次日宣布的事实，即他的言行不代表国民政府，表明汪精卫与其同僚意见不一。1月1日或2日，中央执行委员会常务委员会强调了汪精卫擅自行动的严重性。委员会指责他未经许可擅离职守，发布违背国家利益和政府决定的和平建议，以误导中国人民的方式歪曲敌人的要求，与敌人有关系，并通过其有罪的阴谋活动危及国家的组织。总之，委员会认为汪精卫是在提议中国投降。

在任何其他国家，汪精卫受批评的行为将被视为叛国行为。然而，重庆政府似乎并不认为此事非常严重，因为它只满足于采取相对温和的镇压措施。这并非汪精卫第一次被政府和国民党禁止；他以前的谴责并没有阻止他在一段时间后再次在政府和党的决策层中占据一席之地，甚至被召去领导政府。

然而，他的宣言中的弱点已被中央执行委员会的同僚清楚揭露。在战争时期，政治家擅自决定求和，或通过其阴谋分裂或削弱受托保卫国家的政府，这是不可接受的。除非应政府要求，否则他与敌人建立关系也是同样奇怪的。另一方面，重庆政府说得对，汪精卫通过将近卫亲王和有田八郎先生关于维护中国主权的保证呈现为真诚的，来误导人民，而日本声称要在远东建立的“新秩序”将使中国沦为像今天的满洲国那样的奴隶状态。正如汪精卫的同僚所说，接受日本人提出的和平基础等同于投降。

现在，重庆认为它有足够的手段继续战争。不乏久经战阵的士兵，他们将在更有利的条件下作战。他们的装备充足

January 4, 1939.

for a defensive war. The credits from Great Britain and
the United States of America will enable China to maintain
her currency and to purchase war materials.
Wang Ching-wei is now in a foreign land
and will probably continue his intrigues. It is difficult
to say what he hopes to gain thereby. He has asked the
Japanese to withdraw their armies from China. He prefers
to sacrifice Inner Mongolia which will become a Japanese
military bulwark. But the Japanese will not be able to
remain in Inner Mongolia unless their army controls the
Hopei and Shansi railways. Wang Ching-wei seems to have
resigned himself beforehand to that "restriction" which
will be placed on China's sovereignty. It only remains
to be seen whether the Japanese military leaders will
consent to abandon their conquests. They have declared
their intention to hold the strategic points along the
Yangtse River, the Lunghai Railway and the Kin Han Railway.
They also desire to exercise a rigorous control over the
Chinese Army of the future. It is doubtful whether they
will to-day grant Wang Ching-wei the military concessions
he is asking them.
Certain reports from Japanese sources
state that Wang Ching-wei may proceed to Germany and Italy
to persuade the Fuehrer and Mussolini to induce Japan to
make her terms to China less harsh. But Japan did not
join the "axis" only out of sympathy with these regimes
of might, for she had also calculated upon being given a
free hand in the Far East.
According to other sources of information
Wang Ching-wei is willing to collaborate with the Japanese
militarists and to proceed to Nanking to act as Chief of
the Nanking regime. These reports, however, are not
reliable.
In short, Wang Ching-wei's peace movement
has been refuted by the National Government and by Chinese
public opinion. It may be that Wang Ching-wei will
continue his movement for peace; in that case, his only
chance of success depends upon whether he can prevail
upon the Japanese to reduce their claims. However, it
does not seem that the Japanese are disposed to leave out
anything that is essential. Perhaps Japan will be less
exacting in time; but the Chinese Army must preserve its
cohesion and tenacity, while the measures of economic
reprisals about which London and Washington have been
talking so much must be more substantial than mere subjects
for academic discussion by chancellories and newspapers.
Everything depends upon China's resistance.
It is improbable that Wang Ching-wei's new peace movement
will diminish in firmness.

Georges Moresthe.

进行一场防御性战争。来自大不列颠和
美利坚合众国的信贷将使中国能够维持

汪精卫现在身处异国，
可能会继续他的阴谋活动。很难
说他希望由此获得什么。他已要求
日本人将军队撤出中国。他宁愿
牺牲内蒙古，使其成为日本的
军事堡垒。但是，除非日本军队控制
河北和山西的铁路，否则他们将无法
留在内蒙古。汪精卫似乎事先已经
默许了将施加于中国主权之上的那种“限制”。
现在只需看日本军方领导人是否
会同意放弃他们的征服成果。他们已声明
意图占据沿长江、陇海铁路和京汉铁路的
战略要点。他们还希望对未来的
中国军队实行严格控制。目前尚不确定他们
今天是否会给予汪精卫所要求的军事让步。
某些来自日本方面的
报告称，汪精卫可能会前往德国和意大利，
说服元首和墨索里尼促使日本
减轻对华条件的苛刻程度。但日本加入
“轴心国”并非仅仅出于对这些强权政权的
同情，因为她还盘算着在远东
获得行动自由。
根据其他消息来源，
汪精卫愿意与日本
军国主义者合作，并前往南京担任
南京政权的首脑。然而，这些报道并
不可靠。
总之，汪精卫的和平运动
已被国民政府和中国
舆论所驳斥。也许汪精卫会
继续他的和平运动；在这种情况下，他唯一
的成功机会取决于他能否说服
日本人减少他们的要求。然而，看起来
日本人并不打算放弃任何
实质性的东西。也许日本将来会变得不那么
苛刻；但中国军队必须保持其
凝聚力和韧性，而伦敦和华盛顿一直
大谈的经济报复措施，必须比外交部和报纸上的
学术讨论话题更为切实。
一切取决于中国的抵抗。
汪精卫的新和平运动不太可能
减弱其坚定性。

乔治·莫雷斯特（Georges Moresthe）。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JAN 5 1939

Planes Drop Peace Plea

Handbills printed on green and yellow paper were dropped by two Japanese planes all over Shanghai this morning giving the first outright indication of Japan's great affection for Mr. Wang Ching-wei's peace appeal. Two kinds of handbills were dropped from the air, one containing a full text of Mr. Wang's telegram to Chungking, with his picture, while the other reported that China's ambassadors in Paris (Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo), London (Dr. Quo Tai-chi), and Washington (Dr. Hu Shih) had jointly and secretly wired to Chungking asking the government to sue for peace on four principles; (1) Give up Manchuria, (2) Demand retrocession of the foreign settlements and concessions, (3) Retain the name of the National Government as it is recognized all over the world, and (4) Early peace to present spread of communism in China and to save people from further sufferings. The planes went up at 9.45 and remained in the air until 10.30. The handbills were mostly thrown out from the planes north of Soochow creek to allow a stiff wind to blow them into the heart of the International Settlement and French Concession.

1939年1月5日

飞机投下和平呼吁

今天上午，两架日本飞机在上海各地撒下了印有绿色和黄色纸张的传单，首次明确表明日本对汪精卫先生和平呼吁的极大“喜爱”。空中撒下了两种传单，一种包含汪先生发给重庆的电文全文及其照片，另一种则报道称，中国驻巴黎（顾维钧博士）、伦敦（郭泰祺博士）和华盛顿（胡适博士）的大使已联合秘密致电重庆，请求政府基于四项原则求和：(1) 放弃满洲，(2) 要求收回外国租界和租借地，(3) 保留国民政府的名称，因其为全世界所承认，以及 (4) 早日实现和平，以遏制共产主义在中国的蔓延，并使人民免受进一步的苦难。飞机于9点45分起飞，在空中停留至10点30分。传单主要从苏州河以北的飞机上抛出，以便让强劲的风将其吹入公共租界和法租界的中心地带。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
JAN 6 1939

Surrender Leaflets Dropped
Over Shanghai

Mr. Quo Tai-chi Repudiates Responsibility for
Part in Peace Move; Japanese Gesture

Chungking, Jan. 5.
A "MALICIOUS invention" was the description applied by a spokesman of the Chinese Government to the allegation that the Chinese Ambassadors in London, Paris and Washington had sent General Chiang Kai-shek a telegram urging him to accept Mr. Wang Ching-wei's peace proposals.
The allegation in question was made in pamphlets dropped by aeroplanes on Shanghai this morning.
"Because of the unfavourable impression created abroad by Japan's internal difficulties, the Japanese," the spokesman said, "are trying to divert attention by spreading malicious rumours against China."—Reuter.

A telegram describing his peace proposals as a wrong move and urging him to retract them has been sent to Mr. Wang Ching-wei by Mr. Quo Tai-chi, the Chinese Ambassador in London, Reuter learns today. Mr. Quo has been for many years a close friend of Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
Usually well-informed quarters here assert that Mr. Wang Ching-wei is at present staying at a villa "60 miles from Hanoi."
General Li Tsung-jen, the Kwangsi leader, General Liu Wen-hui, Governor of the newly-created province of Sikong, and various public bodies in Yunnan and Hunan have issued statements denouncing Mr. Wang Ching-wei's peace move.
Chinese newsboys in Hongkong, according to Chinese reports from the Colony, are refusing to sell the Nan Hua Jih Pao, a newspaper published under the auspices of Mr. Wang Ching-wei.—Reuter.

Determined to Fight
London, Jan. 5.
The determination of the Chinese people to fight to the bitter end until an equitable and lasting peace could be obtained had been strengthened, declared Mr. Quo Tai-chi, the Chinese Ambassador in London, speaking yesterday at the National Trade Union Club, London.
He said that the whole country was behind the leadership of General Chiang Kai-shek.
Japan's peace terms, Mr. Quo went on, were a fraudulent attempt to make China a vassal state.
Until Japan changed the terms of her policy towards China, there was no alternative for China but to continue her resistance.
While Japan was showing signs of internal disturbance, China had shown none of weakening, and there was "no possibility of surrender."—Reuter.
Leaflets in different colours were dropped yesterday morning into foreign settlements in Shanghai by two Japanese aeroplanes stating that telegrams had secretly been sent to the Chinese Government by Chinese ambassadors in Europe and America replying to the peace proposal and supporting the idea of making peace with Japan. Another type of leaflet had simply Mr. Wang Ching-wei's recent peace proposal printed on them together with Mr. Wang's picture.

The telegrams purporting to have been sent by Dr. Quo Tai-chi, Chinese Ambassador to London, Dr. Wellington Koo, Chinese Ambassador to Paris and Dr. Hu Shih, Chinese Ambassador to Washington, are stated to be dated December 28, 1938. The telegrams contained five points as follow:
1. China must preserve her territorial integrity by all means.
2. Since Manchuria is not Chinese territory but it is the life-line of Japan it is better to recognize Manchoukuo as China is not even yet able to reconstruct her interior.
3. The protracted warfare has caused much trouble to the people of the two countries while Soviet Russia is watching for a chance to act. All intelligent people realize that China is not suitable for communism and Japan is afraid of it like a "snake." In order to avoid extermination it is better for China to tolerate for the time being by making peace.
4. Foreign settlements in China are sources of all sins and even wise foreigners would like to see them abolished. Now that Japan has proposed to abolish them, China should accept the proposal but the consular jurisdiction must also go at the same time. As to the question of allowing the Japanese to domicile in China, a remedy can be obtained by working out legal and political measures.
5. Since it is internationally recognized the name of the National Government of China must be maintained by all means.

Paris Denies Reports
Paris, Jan. 5.
"Contrary to rumours from Shanghai, neither the Chinese Ambassador to France nor the Chinese Embassy in Paris had sent a telegram to General Chiang Kai-shek or to the Chinese Government approving the idea of accepting the Japanese peace proposals outlined on December 22," a Chinese Embassy communiqué announced today.
"The Embassy takes this opportunity to warn the public against such attempts at propaganda aiming at undermining China's determination to resist under General Chiang Kai-shek's leadership until the final victory."—Havas.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》
1939年1月6日

投降传单撒向
上海上空

郭泰祺先生否认参与
和平运动的责任；日本的姿态

重庆，1月5日。
中国政府发言人将所谓中国驻伦敦、巴黎和华盛顿的大使曾致电蒋介石将军，敦促其接受汪精卫先生的和平提议的说法，形容为“恶意的捏造”。
这一指控出现在今天上午由飞机在上海撒下的传单中。
发言人称：“由于日本内部困难在国外造成了不利印象，日本人正试图通过散布针对中国的恶意谣言来转移注意力。”——路透社。

路透社今日获悉，中国驻伦敦大使郭泰祺先生已向汪精卫先生发出一封电报，称其和平提议是错误的举动，并敦促其撤回。郭先生多年来一直是汪精卫先生的密友。
此处通常消息灵通的人士声称，汪精卫目前住在“距河内60英里”的一处别墅中。
广西领袖李宗仁将军、新成立的西康省省长刘文辉将军，以及云南和湖南的各公共团体已发表声明，谴责汪精卫的和平运动。
据来自该殖民地的中文报道，香港的报童拒绝出售《南华日报》，这是一份在汪精卫先生支持下出版的报纸。——路透社。

决心战斗
伦敦，1月5日。
中国驻伦敦大使郭泰祺先生昨日在伦敦全国工会俱乐部发表讲话时宣称，中国人民战斗到底直至获得公正且持久和平的决心已得到加强。
他表示，全国上下都支持蒋介石将军的领导。
郭先生接着说，日本的和平条件是一种企图使中国成为附庸国的欺诈行为。
在日本改变其对华政策条件之前，中国除了继续抵抗外别无选择。
当日本显示出内部动荡的迹象时，中国并未表现出任何削弱，因此“没有投降的可能性”。——路透社。
昨天上午，两架日本飞机向上海的外国租界撒下了不同颜色的传单，声称中国驻欧洲和美国的大使已秘密向中国政府发送电报，回应和平提议并支持与日本媾和的想法。另一种传单仅印有汪精卫先生最近的和平提议及其照片。

据称由中国驻伦敦大使郭泰祺博士、中国驻巴黎大使顾维钧博士和中国驻华盛顿大使胡适博士发出的电报，日期标注为1938年12月28日。电报包含以下五点：
1. 中国必须不惜一切代价保持领土完整。
2. 既然满洲不是中国领土，而是日本的生命线，最好承认满洲国，因为中国甚至尚未能够重建其内地。
3. 长期战争给两国人民带来了许多麻烦，而苏俄正在伺机而动。所有明智的人都意识到中国不适合共产主义，日本像害怕“蛇”一样害怕它。为了避免灭绝，中国最好暂时容忍，通过媾和来解决。
4. 中国的外国租界是一切罪恶的根源，即使是明智的外国人也希望看到它们被废除。既然日本已提议废除它们，中国应接受该提议，但领事裁判权也必须同时取消。至于允许日本人在中国居住的问题，可以通过制定法律和政治措施来获得补救。
5. 既然国际上已予承认，中国国民政府的名称必须不惜一切代价予以保留。

巴黎否认报道
巴黎，1月5日。
“与来自上海的谣言相反，中国驻法国大使或中国驻巴黎大使馆均未向蒋介石将军或中国政府发送过批准接受12月22日概述的日本和平提议想法的电报，”中国驻大使馆今日发布的一份公报宣布。
“大使馆借此机会警告公众警惕此类旨在破坏中国在蒋介石将军领导下抵抗决心直至最终胜利的宣传企图。”——哈瓦斯社。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.

JAN 6 1939

Attempted Wang Coup D'Etat
Said Frustrated By Lung

CHUNGKING, Jan. 5.—(Kuomin).—The important role played by General Lung Yun, Chairman of the Yunnan Provincial Government, in frustrating an attempted coup d'etat of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, expelled Deputy General Executive of the Kuomintang, is praised in official circles here.

It is stated that, before his flight to Hanoi, Indo-China, Mr. Wang had a lengthy conversation with General Lung Yun, at Kunming (Yunnanfu), provincial capital of Yunnan.

Mr. Wang tried to persuade the Yunnan leader to stage a coup in Yunnan so as to force the Government to accept Mr. Wang's so-called peace proposal. If Yunnan had turned against the Central Government, it is pointed out, it would have cut China's only route of communications with the outside world for the transport of arms and ammunition.

General Lung, it is learnt, flatly and categorically rejected Mr. Wang's ideas, and sent an urgent telegram to General Chiang Kai-shek informing him of Mr. Wang's attempt.

The text of General Lung's historic telegram to General Chiang will be made public shortly.

汪氏政变企图
据称被龙云挫败

重庆，1月5日.—（国民通讯社）.—云南省政府主席龙云将军在挫败被开除的国民党副总裁汪精卫先生未遂政变中所发挥的重要作用，受到此地官方圈子的赞扬。

据悉，在逃往印度支那河内之前，汪先生在云南省会昆明（云南府）与龙云将军进行了长时间谈话。

汪先生试图说服这位云南领导人在云南发动政变，以迫使政府接受汪先生所谓的和平提议。指出如果云南反对中央政府，这将切断中国与外界运输武器弹药的唯一交通路线。

据悉，龙将军断然且明确地拒绝了汪先生的想法，并向蒋介石将军发出紧急电报，告知其汪先生的企图。

龙将军致蒋介石将军的历史性电文全文将于不久后公布。

SHANGHAI TIMES
JAN 4 1939

Political Changes Are
Expected In Chungking
To Follow Wang's Move

COMMUNIST PARTY OFFICIAL EXPECTED
TO BE HIS SUCCESSOR AS DEPUTY
HEAD OF THE KUOMINTANG

BUT STRENGTHENING OF GOVERNMENT
SEEN AS ULTIMATE RESULT

Not Generally Believed That Wang Will Join In
With Nanking Or Peking Regimes; Flight Said
Planned Secretly More Than Month Ago

CHUNGKING, Jan. 3.—Important political changes are expected within the next week as a result of the dismissal of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, who held the posts of chairman of the Central Political Council and Deputy General Executive of the Kuomintang.

His successor as Deputy General Executive of the Kuomintang will, it is reported, be a man of known Leftist sympathies.

Although he probably will not be the actual leader of the Communists, his appointment will naturally draw the Communist Party closer into the fold and, according to official quarters here, will "show the solidarity of the Chinese people."

While Mr. Wang's defection caused a certain amount of momentary dismay in political circles here, a recovery followed quickly, without sign of any serious weakening of the Chinese political structure.

**Ultimate Strength**

Mr. Wang Ching-wei's exit will ultimately have the effect of strengthening the power of the Nationalist Government, in the opinion of Chungking diplomatic circles, who have been watching the situation closely.

Mr. Wang Ching-wei, they point out, had some following, but this was greatly weakened lately by his policy, which caused his supporters uneasiness.

"Mr. Wang is better out of the Government than in it," an observer told Reuter, "for he was a source of constant weakness and uncertainty. The prompt action of the Government in disclaiming his manoeuvres has done much to reassure the people."

**No Going Over Expected**

Among the majority of Chinese and foreigners studying the present political situation, it is not generally believed that Mr. Wang intends immediately to join the Nanking or Peking regimes and thus ally himself irrevocably with a venture the success of which is believed in Chinese circles here to be, as yet, far from certain.

He would rather, they think, remain in retirement watching events from a vantage-point where he can exercise his efforts at mediation if such mediation were, in his opinion, feasible.—Reuter.

**Messages From Abroad**

CHUNGKING, Jan 5.—Messages, according to official circles, are pouring in from all parts of China,

1939年1月4日

预计汪精卫出走后
重庆将发生政治变动

预计共产党官员将接任其
国民党副总裁之职

但认为政府力量终将得到加强

人们普遍不相信汪精卫会加入南京或北平政权；据称其出逃于一个多月前秘密策划

重庆，1月3日电。——由于担任中央政治委员会主席及国民党副总裁职务的汪精卫先生被免职，预计下周内将出现重大的政治变动。

据报道，接替他出任国民党副总裁的人选是一位众所周知的左派同情者。

尽管他可能并非共产党的实际领导人，但他的任命自然会使共产党更紧密地融入阵营，且据当地官方人士称，这将“显示中国人民的团结”。

虽然汪先生的叛离在当地的政界引起了一定程度的短暂恐慌，但局势迅速恢复，中国政治结构并未出现任何严重削弱的迹象。

**最终增强实力**

密切关注事态发展的重庆外交界人士认为，汪精卫先生的离去最终将起到加强国民政府权力的作用。

他们指出，汪精卫先生虽有一些追随者，但其政策近期已大大削弱了这些支持者的信心，令其支持者感到不安。

一位观察家对路透社表示：“汪先生离开政府比留在政府里更好，因为他一直是导致软弱和不确定的根源。政府迅速否认其伎俩的做法，在很大程度上安抚了民心。”

**预计不会投敌**

在研究当前政治局势的大多数中外人士中，普遍不相信汪先生打算立即加入南京或北平政权，从而将自己不可挽回地与一个在此间华人圈看来成功尚远未确定的事业绑定在一起。

他们认为，他宁愿保持隐退，从一个有利的位置观察事态发展，以便在他认为可行的情况下施展调解努力。——路透社。

**来自海外的电文**

重庆，1月5日电。——据官方人士称，来自中国各地以及海外的支持中国政府将汪精卫先生开除出国民党决定的电文正纷至沓来，

Flight Secretly Planned
CHUNGKING, Jan 3—Officials

Yesterday's official announcement

"Traitors To The Nation"
CHUNGKING, Jan. 3.—A decree
issued by the Chinese Government
yesterday orders the arrest of all
"traitors to the nation" but does not
indicate which persons are so de-
signated. The belief, however, pre-

new measure is, to a certain ex-
tent, connected with the case of

1939年1月4日

在此方面，政府迅速而严厉的行动被认为消除了汪精卫离开重庆后立即盛行的所有荒诞谣言和猜测。——路透社。

出逃系秘密策划
重庆，1月3日电。——当地官员称，汪精卫先生离开重庆是于一个多月前经过秘密且周密策划的。

当时，他在昆明南开大学就读的儿子们突然离校。在他本人离开之前，汪精卫先生的全家及随从人员，连同他们的行李和书籍，已经启程前往河内。其在当地的寓所只留下一名看守人，表明了他们永不返回的决心。

昨日官方宣布将汪精卫先生开除出国民党并免除其一切职务，这一决定得到了中国新闻界的一致和衷心支持。

各报在表示对汪精卫先生感到惋惜的同时声明：“这对政府和国家而言均非损失。”——路透社。

“国家叛徒”
重庆，1月3日电。——中国政府昨日颁布一项命令，要求逮捕所有“国家叛徒”，但未指明哪些人被如此定性。然而，政界普遍认为，这项新措施在某种程度上与汪精卫案有关，并有人指出，在关于将汪精卫开除出国民党的官方说明中，明确陈述他犯有战时叛国行为。

据该官方说明，此类行为之一包括通过与中国的敌人进行谈判来动摇中国国家的基础。说明接着指出，“国家纪律不能容忍任何公民在战时违背国家政策，党纪也不允许任何党员公开表达对党领导层所采取路线的意见。”因此，鉴于民族团结和不屈的民族意志是赢得战争的必要条件，开除汪精卫是必要的。

值得注意的是，下令逮捕所有“国家叛徒”的法令明确豁免了所有受日本影响的中国政府成员，法令称这些人是在胁迫下行事，并承诺只要他们“回归中央政府怀抱”，即可予以完全赦免。——跨洋通讯社（Transocean）。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN 4 1939

Chungking's Policy Not To
Be Affected By Wang

Central Party Publicity Department Issues
Statement Castigating Improper Action;
"Ideas Of Only Spineless Cowards"

CHUNGKING, Jan. 2.—The Government's determination to pursue its fixed national policy of resistance against Japanese invasion, despite Mr. Wang Ching-wei's aberration was reiterated by the Central Party Publicity Department, in a statement issued yesterday.

The statement says that Mr. Wang Ching-wei's departure from Chungking had not been previously made known to the leaders of the Central Government, and can only be regarded as a personal matter. Even after his departure, he did not formally notify them of his whereabouts.

Moreover, Mr. Wang's action has absolutely nothing to do with the Kuomintang, the National Government, or the Military Affairs Commission, as already pointed out by General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Military Affairs Commission.

With reference to Mr. Wang's proposal for concluding peace with Japan, the statement says that the text of his proposal was first communicated to the press and published in the newspapers before it was telegraphed to the Central authorities—an improper procedure for a man of Mr. Wang's experience.

Only Personal Ideas

Continuing, the statement says that Mr. Wang's proposal represents only his personal ideas, or at most only the ideas of a few spineless cowards who are willing to be utilized as tools of the enemy. The campaign of resistance is however by no means affected by Mr. Wang's personal views. The Government and the people are determined, now as ever, to resist the Japanese to the uttermost.

The Sino-Japanese question, the statement adds, is not one that can be settled in a day or by one or two individuals. The Government, in pursuance of the bequeathed teachings of the last Party Leader (Dr. Sun Yat-sen) and in accordance with the unanimous will of the people, will continue to pursue its fixed national policy, which can not be altered at the pleasure of one or two persons.

Change Of Opinion

The statement recalls that, ever since the Shenyang (Mukden) Incident in 1931, Mr. Wang has always expressed himself in favour of stiff resistance against Japanese invasion. His change of opinion at the present moment is self-contradictory, to say the least.

Referring to Prince Konoye's recent declaration, on which Mr. Wang's peace proposal is based, the statement says that, as already pointed out by Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, the Japanese Premier's declaration is aimed at the extermination of the Chinese nation, and betrays the exhaustion of Japanese resources for continuing the invasion. This is the opportune moment for a Chinese counter-offensive for the recovery of the lost territories.

Throughout his career as a Revolutionary, the statement adds, Mr. Wang has sometimes shown determination and at other times wavered from his course. For him to desert the cause of the Revolution at the present moment when new difficulties are encountered, is indeed a pity. Mr. Wang's mental aberration does not, however, affect the campaign of resistance in the least.

In conclusion, the statement says that in the course of the Revolution, there have often been deserters, as for instance during the monarchical restoration by Yuan Shih-kai and the revolt of Chen Chiung-ming against Dr. Sun Yat-sen. As history shows, however, the action of a few deserters cannot affect the progress of the Revolution. The entire people are supporting General Chiang Kai-shek, as the supreme leader of the nation, in resisting the invaders to the very end, and this resistance can never be broken by the enemy.—Kuo Min.

《字林西报》
1939年1月4日

重庆政策不受汪精卫影响

中央党部宣传部发表声明谴责不当行为；称其仅为“懦夫之见”

重庆，1月2日电。——中央党部宣传部在昨日发表的声明中重申，尽管汪精卫先生行为乖张，政府仍决心坚持既定的抵抗日本侵略的国家政策。

声明称，汪精卫先生离开重庆一事此前并未告知中央政府领导人，只能视为个人事务。即使在他离开后，他也未正式通知他们其行踪。

此外，正如军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军所指出的那样，汪先生的行动与国民党、国民政府或军事委员会绝对无关。

关于汪先生提出的与日本媾和的建议，声明称，该建议的文本在致电中央当局之前，先向新闻界通报并在报纸上发表——这对于像汪先生这样有经验的人来说，是一种不当的程序。

仅代表个人观点

声明继续指出，汪先生的建议仅代表其个人观点，或者至多只代表少数甘愿被敌人利用为工具的软懦弱夫的观点。然而，抗战运动绝不受汪先生个人观点的影响。政府和人民一如既往，决心抵抗日本到底。

声明补充道，中日问题不是一天或由一两个人就能解决的问题。政府秉承已故党领袖（孙中山博士）的遗教，并根据全民的一致意愿，将继续坚持既定的国家政策，该政策不能因一两人的喜好而改变。

观点转变

声明回顾说，自1931年沈阳（奉天）事变以来，汪先生一直主张坚决抵抗日本侵略。他目前的观点转变，至少可以说是自相矛盾的。

提及汪先生和平建议所依据的近卫亲王最近发表的声明，声明指出，正如蒋介石委员长所指出的那样，日本首相的声明旨在灭绝中华民族，并暴露了日本继续侵略的资源枯竭。这是中国发动反攻、收复失地的良机。

声明补充说，汪先生在其革命生涯中，有时表现出决心，有时则偏离轨道。他在遇到新困难之际背离革命事业，确实令人惋惜。然而，汪先生的精神错乱对抗战运动毫无影响。

最后，声明指出，在革命过程中，常有叛逃者出现，例如袁世凯复辟帝制期间以及陈炯明反对孙中山博士的叛乱期间。然而，正如历史所示，少数叛逃者的行为无法影响革命的进程。全体人民支持作为国家最高领袖的蒋介石将军抵抗侵略者到底，这种抵抗绝不会被敌人打破。——《国民新闻》。

1939年1月4日

汪精卫先生受到谴责

“孤军”指挥官的观点

据上海苏州河北侧一座大仓库内顽强抵抗而闻名的一年多前的“孤军”指挥官谢晋元上校昨日向新闻界发表的新年声明透露，中国政府早在五年前就决定了目前对日全面抵抗的政策，无论声名狼藉的国民党政治家汪精卫先生做何事或说何话，都丝毫不会影响该政策。

谢上校正在医院休养，而300多名同志仍被拘禁在胶州路。

据悉谢上校的声明在此间华人中引起了共鸣，据报道，第二批民间军队“慰劳”团即将离开上海前往香港和广东，慰问南方的中国军队。据报道，近期前往浙江的第一批上海军队“慰劳”人员正启程前往西北从事类似工作。

Where Is
Mr. Wang
Ching-wei?

Rumours Of Arrival In
Shanghai Yesterday
Unconfirmed

Considerable speculation was rife
in Shanghai last night as to the
whereabouts of Mr Wang Ching-
wei, following largely-displayed re-
ports in the Chinese evening news-
papers to the effect that he had
arrived here under an assumed

proved futile, although Reuter had
earlier reported from Hongkong

terday was inclined to reject the

《字林西报》

1939年1月4日

汪精卫先生
身在何处？

昨日抵达上海的传闻
未经证实

昨晚，上海各界对汪精卫先生的下落猜测纷纷，这主要是因为中文晚报大幅刊登报道，称他化名乘坐“罗索伯爵号”（Conte Rosso）抵达此地。

尽管路透社早前从香港报道称，殖民地的中文报纸声称汪先生已登上该意大利邮轮并正前往南京，但核实这些报道的所有努力均告失败。路透社补充说，这些报道无法得到证实。

据发给与中国维新政府关系密切的机构“联合通讯社”（United Press of China）的香港电讯称，汪先生不久将访问柏林和罗马，在那里他会见希特勒先生和墨索里尼先生，与他们讨论中日争端。

昨日上海的外国舆论倾向于否定汪先生会与南京或北平政权同流合污并与日本人接触的想法。人们相信，他至少暂时更愿意退出政坛隐居。

ALLEGED MEETING

Chinese Press Continues

Party Chief

Wang Ching-wei, dismissed from all Government and Kuomintang posts on Monday, is now in Shanghai and is residing in the Broadway Mansions, the Hwa Mei Wan Pao said yesterday.

Interviewed by THE CHINA PRESS a representative of the hotel denied that Wang was on the guest list. He also replied in the negative when asked whether Wang was expected there.

Meanwhile, the Chinese press, while continuing its condemnation of Wang for proposing peace talks with Japan, carried conflicting reports as to Wang's whereabouts.

One report bearing a Hongkong date-line, stated that Wang had been busily engaged conferring with Lieut.-Gen. Kenji Doihara, the notorious Japanese arch-plotter, at the consulate of an unnamed nation in the Colony. The subject of discussion, according to the report concerned Wang's participation in the "Provisional Government".

**Wang Said Going North**

Following the conference, Wang and Doihara were said to have boarded a Japanese war vessel which set sail Sunday night for an unknown destination in the North.

While in the North, Wang was expected to confer with Wu Pei-fu who, according to Japanese sources, had consented to participate in the proposed united "government" of the two Japanese-sponsored regimes in North and Central China.

An earlier report in Hongkong asserted that Wang had embarked from the Colony for Shanghai aboard the Italian liner Conte Rosso on Friday. He was reported to be en route to Nanking on invitation extended to him by Wen Chung-yao, puppet "President of the Legislative Yuan".

**Reported Still In Colony**

Another dispatch from the Colony stated that the former Deputy Executive of the Kuomintang was still in Hongkong preparing for a trip to Europe, probably to France or Germany. The report was considered plausible in view of the fact that Wang's ailment necessitated expert medical advice of his personal physicians on the Continent.

Adding more confusion to Wang's whereabouts, Hongkong Chinese papers, according to local reports, carried a Chungking dispatch stating that Wang had denied sending the peace-talk statement to Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek. He was also said to have denied he would participate in the puppet regimes.

Meanwhile, Mr. Chu Min-yi, a member of the Central Executive and for long Wang's close associate, was reported to have left his Shanghai home for Hongkong.

Mr. Chu's relatives informed THE CHINA PRESS, however, that they could not confirm the report nor did they have any knowledge of his whereabouts.

**Gen. Hsieh's Comment**

Joining the chorus of condemnation against Wang's peace overtures, Major-Gen. Hsieh Ching-yuan, famed Commander of the "Doomed Battalion", in a public statement yesterday expressed the opinion that Wang's desertion would have no effect upon armed resistance.

"Mr. Wang's action," he declared, "indicates the dying days of a few individuals whose determination had been shaken and helps to bring about a firmer foundation for political unity and the will to resist."

In a joint telegram to Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek and the Central Executive Committee, local Chinese civic organizations urged the Government drastically to remove elements in the Government who advocate peace with the Japanese. They pledged again their support to the nation for continued resistance.

**Urged Wang's Arrest**

Expressing the opinion that dismissal from Government and Kuomintang posts alone was not sufficient punishment for his "treacherous" act, the Shun Pao in a strongly worded editorial yesterday asked the authorities in Chungking to effect Wang's arrest and bring him to justice.

Furthermore, the editorial asserted, not only Wang but also the whole "Wang cohort" should be tried for having violated the supreme law of the land against traitors.

汪精卫据称
藏身于苏州河以北

然而，关于其
下落的报道相互矛盾

据传在南部
与土肥原会晤

中国报刊继续
谴责这位前国民党领袖

《华美晚报》昨日称，周一被免除所有政府及国民党职务的汪精卫，目前身处上海，并寓居于百老汇大厦（Broadway Mansions）。

本报记者采访该酒店代表时，对方否认汪精卫在住客名单上。当被问及是否预计汪精卫会前来时，他也予以否认。

与此同时，中国报刊在继续谴责汪精卫提议与日本进行和谈的同时，对其下落刊载了相互矛盾的报道。

一则发自香港的报道称，汪精卫一直在忙于与该殖民地某未具名国家领事馆内的日本著名阴谋策划者土肥原贤二（Kenji Doihara）中将进行磋商。据该报道，讨论的主题涉及汪精卫参与“临时政府”事宜。

**据称汪精卫北上**

据悉，会谈结束后，汪精卫与土肥原登上一艘日本军舰，该舰于周日晚启航，前往北方某未知目的地。

在北方期间，预计汪精卫将与吴佩孚会晤。据日方消息来源称，吴佩孚已同意参与拟议中的、由日本支持的华北和华中两个政权联合组成的“政府”。

早前有一则来自香港的报道声称，汪精卫已于周五乘坐意大利邮轮“罗索伯爵号”（Conte Rosso）离开该殖民地前往上海。据报道，他正应伪“立法院院长”温宗尧之邀前往南京。

**据报仍留在殖民地**

另一则来自该殖民地的电报称，这位前国民党副总裁仍留在香港，准备前往欧洲旅行，可能是去法国或德国。鉴于汪精卫的病情需要其在欧洲大陆的个人医生提供专业医疗建议，该报道被认为具有可信度。

据本地报道，香港中文报纸刊登了一则来自重庆的电报，进一步加剧了关于汪精卫下落的混乱局面，该电报称汪精卫否认曾向蒋介石委员长发送和谈声明。据说他还否认将参与伪政权。

与此同时，据报道，中央执行委员会委员、汪精卫长期的亲密盟友褚民谊先生已离开其在上海的寓所前往香港。

然而，褚先生的亲属告知本报，他们无法证实该报道，也不了解他的下落。

**谢将军的评论**

著名“敢死队”指挥官谢晋元少将在昨日的一份公开声明中，加入谴责汪精卫和平试探的行列，并表示认为汪精卫的叛逃不会对武装抵抗产生影响。

他宣称：“汪先生的举动表明，少数意志动摇者已时日无多，这有助于为政治团结和抵抗意志奠定更坚实的基础。”

当地中国民间团体在向蒋介石委员长和中央执行委员会发出的联合电报中，敦促政府彻底清除政府内部主张与日本媾和的分子。他们再次承诺支持国家坚持抵抗。

**呼吁逮捕汪精卫**

《申报》昨日发表措辞严厉的社论，认为仅免除其政府和国民党职务不足以惩罚其“叛国”行为，并呼吁重庆当局逮捕汪精卫并将其绳之以法。

此外，该社论断言，不仅汪精卫，整个“汪派集团”都应因违反国家惩治汉奸的最高法律而受审。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
JAN 3 1939

The Readers'
Forum

Valiant Wang

To the Editor:
The reading of the papers of to-day urges me to beg you to allow me a very little space in your impartial paper to express my admiration for Mr. Wang Chin Wei's valour in seeking peace. In the first place, tribute should be paid to Mr. Wang's indomitable masochism in his heroic attempt to let his motherland be forever tantalized by hostile and sadistic invaders under the protest of peace—a something which is very foreign to the Chinese heart. In the second place, anyone who is not preparing to commit suicide can not refuse to stare and gasp with wonder at Mr. Wang's unconquerable fortitude in plunging himself into a position to be drowned by the popular hatred of all thinking Chinese; and in being practically deaf to the end less threatenings of hot-headed terrorists. The reading of his bold statements compels from me a feeling of admiration and a sense of surprise which mounts some how to a shock. For evidently he has not read Generalissimo Chiang's refusal to consider Prince Konoye's "peace" terms or he would not be so much befooled and paralysed by poisonous propaganda. Or maybe he has read it; but on account of having listened to Japanese propaganda too much, Mr. Wang has forgotten and lost the ability to understand his mother tongue as well as the faculty to love his motherland.
I do not think it necessary for me have to resort to the old saying that we love peace, but we love justice more and that all we want and fight for is the peace of justice. Still more unnecessary and perhaps unworth-while is to assail Mr. Wang's appreciation of Prince Konoye's proposal, as the Generalissimo has clearly explained what that means to us and definitely stated what road China is now and will be travelling.
What Mr. Wang's intention or ambition really is I do not pretend to know and have no humor to guess. All that I want to say is that Mr. Wang can be befooled and paralysed, but not us Chinese students. And if the intellectual salt and moral elite of the country may be justified to express the public will of the people as the Generalissimo has interpreted the Government,—in fact people and government in China are one at present—I like to tell the English reading public that unless we have got what we fight for, we will never give up. When I say this I feel four hundred millions of patriotic compatriots are at my back.
Yours, etc.,
A CHINESE STUDENT.
Dec. 31, 1938.

1939年1月3日

读者论坛

勇敢的汪精卫

致编辑：
阅读今日的报纸促使我恳请贵公正的报纸赐我少许版面，以表达我对汪精卫先生在寻求和平方面的勇气的钦佩。首先，应当致敬汪先生在其英雄般的尝试中表现出的不可征服的受虐狂精神，他试图让祖国在和平的抗议下永远受到敌对且施虐成性的入侵者的戏弄——这与中国人的心灵格格不入。其次，任何不准备自杀的人都不得不惊愕地注视着汪先生将自己置于被所有有思想的中国人的公众仇恨所淹没的境地时所表现出的不可战胜的坚韧；并且他对头脑发热的恐怖分子无休止的威胁几乎充耳不闻。阅读他大胆的声明使我产生了一种钦佩之情和一种惊讶之感，这种惊讶不知何故升级为震惊。因为显然他没有读到蒋委员长拒绝考虑近卫亲王“和平”条款的声明，否则他就不会被有毒的宣传如此愚弄和麻痹。或者也许他读过了；但由于听信日本宣传太多，汪先生已经忘记并丧失了理解母语的能力以及热爱祖国的本能。
我认为没有必要援引那句老话，即我们热爱和平，但我们更热爱正义，我们所追求和为之战斗的是正义的和平。更为不必要且或许不值得的是去抨击汪先生对近卫亲王提议的赏识，因为蒋委员长已经清楚地解释了那对我们意味着什么，并明确陈述了中国现在及未来将走的道路。
我不假装知道汪先生的真实意图或野心，也没有兴致去猜测。我想说的只是，汪先生可能会被愚弄和麻痹，但我们中国学生不会。如果国家的知识精英和道德楷模有理由像蒋委员长诠释政府那样表达公众意愿——事实上，目前在中国人民和政府是一体的——我想告诉英语读者，除非我们得到了我们为之奋斗的东西，否则我们绝不会放弃。说这话时，我感到四亿爱国同胞在我身后支持。
此致，
一名中国学生。
1938年12月31日。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, JAN 3 1939

Wang Ching-wei Said to Have
Planned Revolt in Yunnan

Conflicting Rumours Over Peace Message; Official
Circles Doubt Authenticity; Expulsion From Party

Hongkong, Jan. 2.

MR. Wang Ching-wei, Chairman of the Central Political Council who was dismissed from all his party and Government posts last night, attempted to start a military revolt against Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek in Yunnan province, Chinese reports said here today.

Mr. Wang was said to have attempted to take advantage of reported dissatisfaction in Yunnan province over the extent of military support being received there from Gen. Chiang's headquarters in Chungking. Yunnan leaders were said to have urgently requested Chungking military authorities to strengthen Yunnan defences after the fall of Canton.

Mr. Wang, who was charged with desertion and defiance of Government policy in Chungking last night, was said to have requested Yunnan military leaders to join with him in a revolt against Gen. Chiang to force an early end to the present Sino-Japanese war.

The Chinese reports said Yunnan authorities, although continuing to be dissatisfied with the amount of military support received from Chungking, refused to make an open break with Gen. Chiang. Consequently, Mr. Wang proceeded to Hongkong to make his break with the Generalissimo known there.

Expelled from Party

Neutral observers here pointed out the possibility that the report had been circulated to emphasize Mr. Wang's "guilt" in opposing the set policy of the National Government regarding peace discussions with Japan. Some quarters doubted that dissatisfaction in Yunnan was serious enough to have invited revolt overtures from a man of Mr. Wang's experience. It also was pointed out that Mr. Wang's connections in Chinese military circles, including Yunnan, were not strong.

Mr. Wang was expelled from the Kuomintang and all Government posts last night because of his statement on peace discussions released in Hongkong last week. Mr. Wang advised Generalissimo Chiang to accept Japan's three terms of peace as a basis for discussion if Japan agreed to withdraw all her troops from Chinese territory.—United Press.

Chungking Puzzled

Chungking, Jan. 1.

Chinese official circles decline to comment on the message alleged to have been sent by Mr. Wang Ching-wei to the Chinese Government. Government circles declare that such a message was "never received here," and that they have no means of knowing whether the alleged message actually emanated from Mr. Wang Ching-wei, or from other sources. Therefore they wish to clear up the point before making any official statement.

While it was not unexpected that Mr. Wang Ching-wei should make efforts to negotiate a peaceful solution of the Sino-Japanese conflict, well-informed circles here express surprise that he should make such a move at this juncture.

Ever since the Lukouchiao Incident, and also later, prior to the fall of Nanking, and after the fall of Hankow, it is learned, Mr. Wang Ching-wei made suggestions of peace negotiations.

Each time, however, it is stated, he abided by the decisions of the Generalissimo, and also of other Government leaders, who expressed determination to carry on the war of resistance.

Chinese circles consider that China's position today is very strong, in fact, stronger than at any previous period during the Sino-Japanese hostilities.

This they ascribe to four factors:—

Firstly, the Chinese army has been completely reorganized, and redistributed for prolonged resistance;

Secondly, China's financial position is much more secure as a result of credits from Britain and America;

Thirdly, China's international position is stronger, with "Britain and America becoming sceptical of Japan's assurances to protect Third Party interests in China"; and

Fourthly, China is now more united than ever, with the South-west and North-west provinces "solidly behind General Chiang Kai-shek in their determination to resist Japan's attempts to penetrate deeper into China's interior. Conditions for resistance are claimed to be favourable.

Proposals Unbelievable

Chinese circles here state that it is "understandable if Mr. Wang Ching-wei proposed peace negotiations immediately after the fall of Hankow, when the picture looked darkest for China, but it is quite unbelievable that he should talk peace now, when the situation is just turning for the better for China."

They believe that Mr. Wang Ching-wei's move not only will not be supported by the Government, but will

据称汪精卫
计划在云南发动叛乱

关于和平消息的传闻相互矛盾；官方人士怀疑其真实性；开除党籍

香港，1月2日。

此处今日收到的中文报道显示，中央政治委员会主席汪精卫先生于昨晚被免除所有党和政府职务后，试图在云南省发动针对蒋介石委员长的军事叛乱。

据说汪精卫试图利用云南省对从重庆蒋委员长总部获得的军事支持程度不满的报道。据说在广州沦陷后，云南领导人曾紧急请求重庆军事当局加强云南防务。

昨晚在重庆被指控开小差和违抗政府政策的汪精卫，据说曾请求云南军事领导人与他一起发动反对蒋将军的叛乱，以迫使当前的中日战争早日结束。

中文报道指出，云南当局虽然继续对从重庆获得的军事支持数量表示不满，但拒绝与蒋将军公开决裂。因此，汪精卫前往香港，在那里公开宣布他与委员长的决裂。

被开除出党

此处的中立观察家指出，散布该报道的可能性是为了强调汪精卫在反对国民政府关于与日本进行和平谈判既定政策方面的“罪责”。某些方面怀疑云南的不满情绪是否严重到足以引来像汪先生这样有经验的人提出叛乱邀请。还有人指出，汪先生在中国军界（包括云南）的关系并不牢固。

汪精卫因上周在香港发布的关于和平谈判的声明，于昨晚被开除出国民党并免除所有政府职务。汪精卫建议蒋介石委员长接受日本的三项和平条件作为讨论基础，前提是日本同意将其所有军队撤出中国领土。——合众社。

重庆感到困惑

重庆，1月1日。

中国官方人士拒绝对据称由汪精卫先生发送给中国政府的消息发表评论。政府人士声明，此类消息“从未在此收到”，且他们无法得知所谓消息是否确实出自汪精卫先生或其他来源。因此，他们希望在发表任何官方声明之前澄清这一点。

虽然汪精卫先生努力谈判解决中日冲突并不出人意料，但此处的知情人士表示惊讶，他竟然在此时采取此类行动。

据悉，自卢沟桥事变以来，以及后来在南京沦陷之前和汉口沦陷之后，汪精卫先生都曾提出过和平谈判的建议。

然而，据说每次他都遵从蒋委员长及其他政府领导人的决定，这些领导人表达了坚持抗战的决心。

中国各界认为，中国目前的地位非常稳固，事实上比中日敌对行动期间的任何以往时期都要强大。

他们将此归因于四个因素：—

第一，中国军队已完成重组，并重新部署以进行持久抵抗；

第二，由于获得英国和美国的信贷，中国的财政状况更加稳固；

第三，中国的国际地位更强，“英国和美国对日本保护在华第三方利益保证的怀疑态度日益增加”；以及

第四，中国现在比以往任何时候都更加团结，西南和西北各省“坚定地支持蒋蒋介石将军抵抗日本试图进一步渗透中国内地的决心”。据称抵抗条件有利。

提议令人难以置信

此处的中国各界表示，“如果在汉口刚沦陷、中国局势看起来最黑暗的时候，汪精卫先生提出和平谈判是可以理解的，但现在局势正对中国好转，他却谈论和平，这完全令人难以置信。”

他们认为，汪精卫先生的举动不仅不会得到政府的支持，而且将

汪精卫先生。

遭到全国人民的强烈谴责。然而，他们补充说，他们仍然怀疑该消息是否确实出自汪精卫先生。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS, JAN 3 1939

Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Chairman of the Central Political Council and Deputy General Executive of the Kuomintang, from the Party permanently. At the same time, a statement, addressed to the Chinese and foreign public, was issued, which vigorously denounced Mr. Wang Ching-wei's so-called "peace movement" as completely violating Party discipline.

The statement reaffirmed the firm determination of the Kuomintang and the Chinese Government to follow the policy enunciated by General Chiang Kai-shek, in his address at the weekly memorial service, on December 26, in which he reiterated China's intention to carry on her war of resistance to the end. Any person advocating a programme contrary to the principles contained in General Chiang Kai-shek's speech, the statement added, would be opposed and denounced by the Kuomintang.

Leniency Move Vetoed

At yesterday's meeting, General Chiang Kai-shek advocated a lenient attitude towards Mr. Wang, proposing that he be given friendly advice first, then a warning and finally be expelled from the Party only if he did not heed the warning.

Despite this, however, Reuter was authoritatively informed that the Kuomintang leaders were "very indignant" at Mr. Wang's "peace message" and unanimously adopted a resolution for his permanent expulsion from the Party. It was also stated that the Elder Statesmen, Messrs. Wu Tze-hui and Chang Chi, who had been working for nearly a generation with Mr. Wang Ching-wei in the Kuomintang Revolutionary movement, were very bitter in their denunciation of him.

It was learned here that Mr. Wang Ching-wei's message was dated December 29, but was circulated to the Hongkong press on the following day by Mr. Lin Peh-sen, a close associate of Mr. Wang, and reached Chungking yesterday morning. The Generalissimo immediately summoned a meeting of the Kuomintang leaders, despite the New Year holiday, at which he, himself, presided.

The National Government office also issued an official mandate, ordering the arrest and punishment of all persons participating in regimes established by the Japanese, as "traitors."—Reuter.

Mr. Chow En-lai's Views

Mr. Chow En-lai, one of the most prominent leaders of the Chinese Communist Party, told Reuter today that the "peace move" made by Mr. Wang Ching-wei came as no surprise to him since, "in my twenty years' association with Mr. Wang, I have always known him to be a quitter."

Mr. Chow, who will be remembered for the role he played in the Sian incident, said that Mr. Wang, during his entire political career, had "frequently changed alignments." Mr. Wang, he declared, had worked with the Communists at Hankow in 1927, had joined the rebellion of Yen Hsi-shan and Feng Yu-hsiang against General Chiang Kai-shek, and had also joined Lu Han-min in the Canton revolt.

Every time, however, Mr. Chow En-lai continued, Mr. Wang had betrayed his colleagues as soon as the going was difficult and, being an opportunist, had always pursued the line of least resistance."

First Moves of "Peace Talk"

Mr. Wang's first move towards negotiation with the Japanese, according to Mr. Chow, was made in the interview he gave Reuter immediately after the fall of Canton, and just before the fall of Hankow, last October, when he made a statement expressing China's readiness to discuss peace with Japan.

This statement, Mr. Chow pointed out, was vigorously denounced by all the commanding officers who participated in a military conference at Nanyo, in Hunan, in November. General Chang Fa-kwei, who for many years was a close associate of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, and who was at present directing operations in Kwangtung, was among those who bitterly attacked Mr. Wang on that occasion.

Mr. Chow revealed that at the National People's Congress, which met in Chungking in November, a close associate of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, in an address, said that assistance from Great Britain, the United States, France and Russia could not be depended upon, and that China must seek a peaceful solution of her conflict with Japan through the assistance of Germany and Italy. Mr. Chow also alleged that Mr. Wang had made overtures to the Japanese through his agent in Hongkong, who had "visited Tokyo at least once."

Loss of Following Alleged

Mr. Wang's action, he added, would neither affect China's internal solidarity nor the strength of her resistance.

"Mr. Wang," he went on, "has now practically no following in the Party, in the Government or the Army, except for a few associates like Tseng Chung-min and Chu Ming-yi, who never amounted to anything." Mr. Chow En-lai expressed the belief that it was doubtful whether Ku Meng-yu or Chen Kung-po would join Mr. Wang Ching-wei.

In conclusion, he absolutely refuted the rumour that Mr. Wang's trip to Hongkong might have been undertaken on an understanding with General Chiang Kai-shek. "I know, and am confident," he said, "that General Chiang Kai-shek has absolutely nothing to do with Mr. Wang Ching-wei's action."

London Surprised

London, Jan. 1.
Chinese circles in London are inclined to regret Mr. Wang Ching-wei's reported "peace" message to General Chiang Kai-shek, lest it should create an unjustified impression of disunity among members of the Chinese Cabinet, Reuter learns today.

Leaving aside the dislike by Mr. Wang's group of the Government's association with Communists, emphasis is laid on the overwhelming support given to General Chiang by all other sections of the Chinese people.

Attention is also drawn to General Chiang Kai-shek's emphatic repudiation of Japanese peace offers and the backing his attitude has received in China. The view is expressed that no compromise with Japan appears possible.

The idea of China joining an economic bloc with Japan and Manchoukuo is equally rejected, because it is thought that it would put China completely under Japanese control.

The strength of Mr. Wang Ching-wei's following is questioned by his critics, but rumours that he might join one of the Japanese-sponsored governments in Nanking or Peiping are entirely scouted.

It is thought more probable that if the present move fails, he will try to get more favourable terms from Japan to submit to General Chiang Kai-shek.

Japanese Silent

TOKYO, Jan. 1.—(Reuters).—Japanese officialdom declines at present to comment on Mr. Wang Ching-wei's alleged "peace" message to General Chiang Kai-shek.

Although giving it great prominence, the Japanese press has also hitherto been silent, possibly awaiting an official lead, in view of the fact that Mr. Wang Ching-wei is said to have misrepresented Prince Konoye's proposals on several vital points.

《字林西报》，1939年1月3日

国民党中央政治委员会主席、国民党副总裁汪精卫先生被永久开除出党。同时，发表了一份致中外公众的声明，强烈谴责汪精卫先生所谓的“和平运动”完全违反党纪。

该声明重申，国民党及中国政府坚定决心遵循蒋介石将军在12月26日每周纪念周演讲中所阐明的政策，他在演讲中重申中国将抗战到底的意图。声明补充说，任何提倡与蒋介石将军演讲中所含原则相悖的方案的人，都将遭到国民党的反对和谴责。

宽大处理提议被否决

在昨日的会议上，蒋介石将军主张对汪先生采取宽大态度，提议先给予友好劝告，然后提出警告，只有在其不听警告的情况下，才最终将其开除出党。

尽管如此，路透社还是从权威方面获悉，国民党领导人对汪先生的“和平通电”感到“非常愤慨”，并一致通过决议，将其永久开除出党。据称，元老吴稚晖和张继两位先生，他们与汪精卫先生在国民党革命运动中合作了近一代人的时间，也对汪进行了严厉的谴责。

此处获悉，汪精卫先生的通电日期为12月29日，但由汪的亲信林柏生先生于次日分发给香港报界，并于昨天上午抵达重庆。尽管正值新年假期，委员长立即召集国民党领导人开会，并亲自主持会议。

国民政府办公厅还发布了一道正式命令，下令逮捕并惩罚所有参与日本建立的政权的人员，视其为“汉奸”。——路透社。

周恩来先生的观点

中国共产党最杰出的领导人之一周恩来先生今天告诉路透社，汪精卫先生的“和平举动”对他来说并不意外，因为“在我与汪先生二十年的交往中，我一直知道他是一个半途而废者（quitter）。”

因在西安事变中所扮演的角色而为人们所铭记的周先生表示，汪先生在整个政治生涯中“经常改变阵营”。他宣称，汪先生曾在1927年在汉口与共产党人合作，随后加入了阎锡山和冯玉祥反对蒋介石将军的叛乱，还曾加入胡汉民在广州的叛乱。

然而，周恩来先生继续说道，每次一旦局势困难，汪先生就背叛他的同事，作为一个机会主义者，他总是采取阻力最小的路线。”

“和谈”的初步举动

据周先生称，汪先生迈向与日本谈判的第一步，是在去年10月广州沦陷后、汉口沦陷前接受路透社采访时做出的，当时他发表声明，表示中国愿意与日本讨论和平。

周先生指出，这一声明遭到了11月在湖南南岳参加军事会议的所有指挥官的强烈谴责。多年来一直是汪精卫先生亲密伙伴、当时正在广东指挥作战的张发奎将军，也是在那次场合严厉抨击汪先生的人之一。

周先生透露，在11月于重庆召开的国民参政会上，汪精卫先生的一位亲信在发言中表示，不能依赖英国、美国、法国和俄罗斯的援助，中国必须通过德国和意大利的援助来寻求解决与日本冲突的和平方案。周先生还指控汪先生通过其在香港的代理人向日本人示好，该代理人“至少访问过东京一次”。

据称失去追随者

他补充说，汪先生的行动既不会影响中国的内部团结，也不会影响其抵抗力量。

他接着说：“汪先生在党内、政府内或军队中现在实际上已没有追随者，除了像曾仲鸣和朱明夷这样几个从未成气候的亲信之外。”周恩来表示，他怀疑顾孟余或陈公博是否会加入汪精卫先生一方。

最后，他绝对驳斥了这样一种谣言，即汪先生前往香港可能是基于与蒋介石将军的默契。“我知道，并且确信，”他说，“蒋介石将军与汪精卫先生的行动绝对没有任何关系。”

伦敦感到惊讶

伦敦，1月1日。
路透社今日获悉，伦敦华人圈子倾向于对汪精卫先生 reportedly 向蒋介石将军发出的“和平”通电表示遗憾，担心这会给人们造成中国内阁成员之间不团结的错误印象。

撇开汪派集团对政府与共产党人结盟的反感不谈，人们强调的是中国所有其他阶层对蒋介石将军的压倒性支持。

人们还注意到蒋介石将军坚决拒绝日本的和平提议，以及他的态度在中国得到的支持。有观点认为，与日本妥协似乎是不可能的。

中国与日本及满洲国加入经济集团的想法同样遭到拒绝，因为人们认为这将使中国完全处于日本的控制之下。

批评者质疑汪精卫先生追随者的实力，但有关他可能加入南京或北平某个日本赞助的政府的谣言则完全被斥为无稽之谈。

人们认为更有可能的是，如果目前的举动失败，他将试图从日本获得更有利的条件，以便向蒋介石将军屈服。

日本保持沉默

东京，1月1日。（路透社）。日本官方目前拒绝对汪精卫先生 reportedly 向蒋介石将军发出的“和平”通电发表评论。

尽管日本报纸给予了极大关注，但迄今为止一直保持沉默，可能是因为汪精卫先生据说在近卫公爵提议的几个关键问题上进行了歪曲，因此可能在等待官方的指引。

SHANGHAI TIMES.    JAN 3 1939

MR. WANG CHING-WEI
IS EXPELLED FROM
THE KUOMINTANG

*Emergency Session Held*
*At Chungking By Chiang*
*Kai-shek's Instructions*

Generalissimo Himself Presides At Meeting To
Condemn Deputy General Executive For
Making Peace Overtures To Japan

CHOW EN-LAI, RED LEADER. SAYS HE
ALWAYS KNEW WANG AS "QUITTER"

CHUNGKING, Jan. 2.—An emergency joint plenary session
of the Central Executive and Control Committees of the Kuo-
mintang decided, yesterday afternoon, to expel Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, Chairman of the Central Political Council and
Deputy General Executive of the Kuomintang, from the Party
permanently.

At the same time, a statement, addressed to the Chinese
and foreign public, was issued, which vigorously denounced
Mr. Wang Ching-wei's so-called "peace movement" as com-
pletely violating Party discipline.

The statement reaffirmed the firm determination of the
Kuomintang and the Chinese Government to follow the policy
enunciated by General Chiang Kai-shek, in his address at the
weekly memorial service, on December 26, in which he reiter-
ated China's intention to carry on her war of resistance to
the end.

It was learnt here that Mr.
Wang Ching-wei's message was
dated December 29, but was cir-
culated to the Hongkong press on
the following day by Mr. Lin Peh-
sen, a close associate of Mr. Wang,
and reached Chungking yesterday
morning.

The Generalissimo immediately
summoned a meeting of the Kuo-
mintang leaders, despite the New
Year holiday, at which he himself,
presided.

The National Government office
also issued an official mandate,
ordering the arrest and punishment
of all persons participating in re-
gimes established by the Japanese,
as "traitors."—Reuter.

Any person advocating a pro-
gramme contrary to the principles
contained in General Chiang Kai-
shek's speech, the statement added,
would be opposed and denounced
by the Kuomintang.

At yesterday's meeting, General
Chiang Kai-shek advocated a lenient
attitude towards Mr. Wang, pro-
posing that he be given friendly
advice first, then a warning and
finally be expelled from the Party
only if he did not heed the warn-
ing.

Despite this, however, Reuter was
authoritatively informed that the
Kuomintang leaders were "very in-
dignant" at Mr. Wang's "peace
message" and unanimously adopted
a resolution for his permanent ex-
pulsion from the Party.

It was also stated that the Elder
Statesmen, Messrs. Wu Tze-hui and
Chang Chi, who had been working
for nearly a generation with Mr.
Wang Ching-wei in the Kuomintang
Revolutionary movement, were
very bitter in their denunciation of
him.

Red Leader's Denunciation
CHUNGKING, Jan. 2.—Mr. Chow
En-lai, one of the most prominent
leaders of the Chinese Communist
Party, told Reuter to-day that the
"peace move" made by Mr. Wang
Ching-wei came as no surprise to
him since, "in my 20 years' associa-
tion with Mr. Wang, I have always
known him to be a quitter."

汪精卫先生
被开除出
国民党

*奉蒋介石指示*

委员长亲自主持会议

中共领袖周恩来说

SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN 3 1939

Mr. Chow who will be remembered for the role he played in the Sian incident, said that Mr. Wang, during his entire political career had "frequently changed alignments."
Mr. Wang, he declared, had worked with the Communists at Hankow in 1927, had joined the rebellion of Yen Hsi-shan and Feng Yu-hsiang against General Chiang Kai-shek, and had also joined Hu Han-min in the Canton revolt.
Every time, however, Mr. Chow En-lai continued, Mr. Wang had "betrayed his colleagues as soon as the going was difficult and, being an opportunist, had always pursued the line of least resistance."
Mr. Wang's first move towards negotiation with the Japanese, according to Mr. Chow, was made in the interview he gave Reuter immediately after the fall of Canton, and just before the fall of Hankow, last October, when he made a statement expressing China's readiness to discuss peace with Japan.
This statement, Mr. Chow pointed out, was vigorously denounced by all the commanding officers who participated in a military conference at Nanyo, in Hunan, in November.
General Chang Fa-kwei, who for many years was a close associate of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, and who was at present directing operations in Kwangtung, was among those who bitterly attacked Mr. Wang on that occasion.
Mr. Chow revealed that at the National People's Congress, which met in Chungking in November, a close associate of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, in the course of an address, said that assistance from Great Britain, the United States, France and Russia could not be depended upon, and that China must seek a peaceful solution of her conflict with Japan through the assistance of Germany and Italy.

Agent's Visit To Tokyo
Mr. Chow also alleged that Mr. Wang had made overtures to the Japanese through his agent in Hongkong, who had "visited Tokyo at least once."
Mr. Wang's action, he added, would neither affect China's internal solidarity nor the strength of her resistance.
"Mr. Wang," he went on," has now practically no following in the Party, in the Government or the Army, except for a few associates like Tseng Chung-min and Chu Ming-yi, who never amounted to anything."
Mr. Chow En-lai expressed the belief that it was doubtful whether Ku Meng-yu or Cheng Kung-po would join Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
In conclusion, he absolutely refuted the rumour that Mr. Wang's trip to Hongkong might have been undertaken on an understanding with General Chiang-Kai-shek.
"I know, and am confident," he said, "that General Chiang Kai-shek has absolutely nothing to do with Mr. Wang Ching-wei's action."—Reuter.

Not Unexpected
CHUNGKING, Jan. 1.—While it was not unexpected that Mr. Wang Ching-wei should make efforts to negotiate a peaceful solution of the Sino-Japanese conflict, well-informed circles here express surprise that he should make such a move at this juncture.
Ever since the Lukouchiao Incident, and also later, prior to the fall of Nanking, and after the fall of Hankow, it is learnt, Mr. Wang Ching-wei made suggestions of peace negotiations.

Resolved To Resist
Each time, however, it is stated, he abided by the decisions of the Generalissimo, and also of other Government leaders, who expressed determination to carry on the war of resistance.
Chinese circles consider that China's position to-day is very strong, in fact, stronger than at any previous period during the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
This they ascribe to four factors:
First, the Chinese Army has been completely reorganized, and redistributed for prolonged resistance;
Secondly, China's financial position is much more secure as a result of credits from Britain and America;
Thirdly, China's international position is stronger, with "Britain and America becoming sceptical of Japan's assurances to protect Third Party interests in China"; and
Fourthly, China is now more united than ever, with the South-West and North-West Provinces solidly behind General Chiang Kai-shek in their determination to resist Japan's attempts to penetrate deeper into China's interior—conditions for such resistance are claimed to be favourable.
Chinese circles here state that it is "understandable if Mr. Wang Ching-wei proposed peace negotiations immediately after the fall of Hankow, when the picture looked darkest for China, but it is quite unbelievable that he should talk peace now, when the situation is just turning for the better for China."
They believe that Mr. Wang Ching-wei's move not only will not be supported by the Government, but will also be vigorously denounced by the entire nation.
They add, however, that they still doubt if the message actually emanated from Mr. Wang Ching-wei.—Reuter.

"Splashed" By Tokyo Press
TOKYO, Jan. 1.—Mr. Wang Ching-wei's alleged "peace" message to General Chiang Kai-shek was received in Tokyo early yesterday morning, and was "splashed" in the morning papers.
There was no comment yesterday, however, on the statement, owing to the fact that the Japanese nation was engrossed in New Year celebrations.—Reuter.

Japanese Officialdom Silent
TOKYO, Jan. 1.—Japanese officialdom declines at present to comment on Mr. Wang Ching-wei's alleged "peace" message to General Chiang Kai-shek.
Although giving it great prominence, the Japanese press has also hitherto been silent, possibly awaiting an official lead, in view of the fact that Mr. Wang Ching-wei is said to have misrepresented Prince Konoye's proposals on several vital points.—Reuter.
